picks.title: Four-Loop Nonsinglet Splitting Functions in QCD
picks.abstract: The scale evolution of parton distributions is governed by splitting functions. We compute the four-loop splitting functions in perturbative QCD that control the evolution of quark nonsinglet distributions. We confirm previous partial results and obtain, for the first time, fully analytic expressions for all nonsinglet contributions at this order. These allow us to extract the analytic form of the four-loop virtual and rapidity anomalous dimensions entering logarithmic resummation. We provide precise numerical representations of the splitting functions suitable for parton evolution.

picks.title: Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome
picks.abstract: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is a common cause of acute hypoxemic respiratory failure in patients with pneumonia, sepsis, aspiration of gastric contents, severe trauma, or other inciting triggers. Although the definition of the syndrome has evolved over the past several decades, the core elements (acute onset, hypoxemia, and bilateral radiographic opacities) remain consistent. Critical components of management include identification and treatment of the underlying cause of ARDS as well as avoidance of ventilator-induced lung injury and volume overload. Ongoing areas of controversy include the best strategy for supporting nonintubated patients, personalization of positive end-expiratory pressure, the role of innovative ventilatory strategies, and the use of glucocorticoids. New research suggests that precision medicine approaches to ARDS management that focus on discrete biologic, radiographic, or physiological subphenotypes may improve outcomes, and prospective trials of these approaches are ongoing.

picks.title: Quantum-classical separation in bounded-resource tasks arising from measurement contextuality
picks.abstract: Quantum phenomena can be exploited to tackle certain problems beyond the reach of classical approaches. In this study, we focus on coordinated decision-making among many players without communication, the study of which, on current quantum processors, has remained elusive. Using a superconducting qubit processor, we show that quantum contextuality enables certain tasks to be performed with success probabilities beyond classical limits. With a few qubits, we illustrate quantum contextuality with the magic square game and quantify it through a Bell-Kochen-Specker inequality violation. To examine many-body contextuality, we implement the N -player Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger game and separately solve a two-dimensional hidden linear function problem, advancing the state of the art on fidelity and system size in both tasks. Our work introduces benchmarking of quantum processors using contextuality-based algorithms.

picks.title: Zero-shot de novo design of a metalloenzyme
picks.abstract: De novo design of enzymes is a frontier challenge, requiring consideration of catalytic mechanism and optimization across biochemical and biophysical criteria. Here, we present dEVA (design by EVolutionary Algorithm), a multi-objective protein design method built on principles drawn from evolutionary biology. We apply dEVA to the zero-shot, de novo design of metalloenzymes by optimizing the coordination sphere of catalytic metals. We characterize a bi-zinc metalloenzyme that exhibits promiscuous hydrolytic activity towards both phosphomonoesters and phosphodiesters. This design achieves a rate enhancement ((k cat /K M )/k w ) of up to 3 x 10 13 relative to the uncatalyzed reaction, comparable to characterized natural phosphatases. Structural characterization via x-ray crystallography and absorption spectroscopy supports the design of a de novo active site. These results demonstrate that de novo enzymes can be designed without pre-specified motifs, natural templates, or evolutionary information.

picks.title: Combinatorial Approach to Circuit Complexity: From Approximate Quantum Codes to Lieb-Schultz-Mattis Constraints
picks.abstract: Approximate quantum error correction (AQEC) provides a versatile framework for both quantum information processing and probing many-body entanglement. We reveal a fundamental tension between the error-correcting power of an AQEC and the hardness of code state preparation. More precisely, through a novel application of the Lovász local lemma, we establish a fundamental tradeoff between local indistinguishability and circuit complexity, showing that orthogonal short-range entangled states must be distinguishable via a local operator. These results offer a powerful tool for exploring quantum circuit complexity across diverse settings. As applications, we derive stronger constraints on the complexity of AQEC codes with transversal logical gates and establish strong complexity lower bounds for W state preparation. Our framework also provides a novel perspective for systems with Lieb-Schultz-Mattis type constraints.

picks.title: The Life and Death of Stars that Capture Primordial Black Holes
picks.abstract: Primordial black holes (PBHs) in the asteroid mass window (10 17 –10 23 g) remain viable dark matter candidates and can be captured by stars. We develop the first global framework for the evolution of stars that capture PBHs, combining analytic calculations, stellar evolution models, 3D general-relativistic magnetohydrodynamic simulations, and Monte Carlo population synthesis. We find that the fate of these systems bifurcates: PBHs that form an accretion disk before consuming the host drive explosive disruption, whereas PBHs captured too late or growing too slowly consume the star quietly. Capture is dominated by three-body interactions with planetary or stellar companions. For a solar-type host with a Jupiter analog, inspiral within a main-sequence lifetime requires M BH crit ≳ 1 0 22 g , while lighter PBHs generally require tighter companions. Once deposited at the center, the PBH grows through inefficient quasi-spherical Bondi accretion; if it reaches the angular-momentum threshold before consuming the host, the inflow circularizes into a disk. Our Monte Carlo calculations yield sizable quiet-consumption and explosive-disruption populations, with final PBH masses M BH ∼ 0.01–1 M ⊙ and disk-forming PBH spins a * ≈ 0.8. Disk formation is the point of no return: disk winds and relativistic jets of ∼10 45 –10 50 erg s −1 disrupt the star within minutes. The resulting transients may include a ∼day-long UV/blue signal, radio afterglow, and, if the jet escapes, an X-ray-flash (XRF)/low-luminosity gamma-ray-burst (llGRB) signal. For an O ( 1 ) PBH dark matter fraction and optimistic capture assumptions, the event rate can reach that of llGRBs. The low-mass, high-spin remnants offer a complementary PBH probe and possible source for subsolar black hole mergers.

picks.title: Multiscale Modeling of Virus Capsid Self-Assembly Reveals How Small Molecule Antivirals Can Redirect Assembly Pathways and Products
picks.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
picks.abstract: Controlling the assembly of a virus capsid, a regular complex of hundreds of subunits, has applications for development of antivirals and for development of nanocontainers. Recent work has shown that a class of small molecules called capsid assembly modulators (CAMs) is promising for treating Hepatitis B virus (HBV). CAMs bind to HBV capsid proteins and alter their self-assembly, leading to nonfunctional and malformed structures. The mechanisms by which CAMs alter capsid assembly remain unclear. Here, we use a kinetic Monte Carlo (KMC) model for HBV capsid assembly to simulate how CAMs affect this complex reaction. The model is parametrized from all-atom simulations, resulting in unprecedented correlation between simulation and biochemical and structural observations. Simulations reproduce the effect of CAMs on experimental assembly products and their distributions. By analyzing assembly trajectories, we clarify the roles of thermodynamics and kinetics in determining assembly products, identify assembly mechanisms, and predict the key intermediates that lead to either capsids or malformed structures. Our findings enhance our fundamental understanding of capsid assembly, help advance the development of CAMs as a treatment for HBV and, more broadly, inform efforts to direct self-assembly pathways toward specific products.

picks.title: Time-dependent Cosmic-Ray Escape from Wind Bubbles: Hard Spectra Formation
picks.abstract: Wind-driven bubbles are dynamic systems that can accelerate cosmic rays, depending on their physical properties, up to very high energies (VHE). We investigate how a time-dependent description of the particle transport may impact the escaping cosmic-ray flux. The wind bubble system is modeled as spherically symmetric. Cosmic rays are continuously injected at the position of the termination shock and propagate through advection and diffusion until the escape at the time-dependent position of the forward shock, which is treated as a free escape boundary. The one-dimensional spherical time-dependent transport equation is solved by transforming it into the corresponding set of stochastic differential equations (SDEs) and integrated with a modified version of the open source cosmic-ray propagation framework CRPropa. We find that, during the wind driven phase, the downstream escaping spectra from wind bubbles can be harder than ∼ E −2 , the conventional expectation from diffusive shock acceleration (DSA). Depending on the turbulence model, the initial energy spectrum can be significantly suppressed at the lowest energies, which could be an observable feature to distinguish between different turbulence realizations. This effect could lead to an efficient confinement of low energy particles, potentially leading to observable implication in terms of multimessenger radiation and cosmic-ray accumulated grammage within the bubble.

picks.title: Resolving Ultrafast Electronic and Chiral Structural Dynamics That Govern Circularly Polarized Luminescence from Eu(III) Antenna Complexes
picks.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
picks.abstract: Circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) from chiral molecules and materials has promising applications in display technology, optical sensing, and quantum information science. However, luminescent-state configurations that approach the maximum degree of circular polarization in emission have only been achieved in exceptional cases, most notably in Eu(III) antenna complexes. An open challenge is the understanding and suppression of detrimental relaxation dynamics of the CPL-active state, which can distort carefully designed ground-state configurations and quench luminescence. We now resolve these processes for the prototypical Eu(III) antenna complex CsEu((+,−)-hfbc)4 (hfbc = 3-heptafluorobutyrylcamphorate) by mapping its complete electronic and chiral structural evolution with ultrafast circular dichroism spectroscopy. Combined with transient absorption measurements and electronic structure calculations, we unravel the intramolecular energy transfer from the helically arranged antenna ligands to the emissive metal ion, and extract the stereochemical configuration of all involved excited states through their ligand-centered circular dichroism. We find that population transfer proceeds from delocalized singlet excitonic states via a ligand-localized triplet, while a parallel singlet exciton trapping channel unexpectedly quenches luminescence. Remarkably, excitation of the luminescent Eu(III) ion increases the helical twist of the ligand sphere by 2.7 ± 1.3° toward an ideal square-antiprismatic geometry, where the CPL performance is most favorable. The excited 4f-orbitals thus drive non-negligible changes in the primary coordination sphere, challenging common assumptions in 4f coordination chemistry and elucidating the need for ligand antenna rigidification to maximize…

picks.title: Deadly Disease, Fear, and Ostracism in the Credit Market
picks.abstract: This paper exploits the 2014 U.S. Ebola outbreak as a natural experiment to examine how fear distorts mortgage credit allocation. We find a 3.8-percentage-point increase in mortgage denial rates for Black applicants during the outbreak, despite negligible infection risk. Approved Black borrowers have stronger credit profiles and lower default rates, yet are less likely to receive loan modifications when delinquent. These effects are absent in algorithm-driven FinTech lending and reverse quickly postoutbreak—patterns inconsistent with statistical discrimination. Robustness tests rule out alternative explanations related to political cycles, labor market impacts, applicant pool composition changes, and bank financial conditions. Consistent with diagnostic expectation theory, higher exposure to Ebola fear does not result in a significant learning effect during the COVID-19 pandemic. more.title: Topological Quantum Criticality in the Quasiperiodic Cluster Ising Chain
more.abstract: Topological classifications of quantum critical systems have recently attracted growing interest, as they go beyond the traditional paradigms of condensed matter and statistical physics. However, such classifications remain largely unexplored in aperiodic environments, particularly under quasiperiodic modulations. In this Letter, we uncover a family of topological quasiperiodic fixed points with critical scalings intermediate between the clean and infinite-randomness limits. By exactly solving the quasiperiodic cluster Ising chain, we demonstrate that all phase boundaries separating quasiperiodically modulated phases are governed by topological Ising-like fixed points unique to strongly modulated quasiperiodic systems. Although their local bulk critical properties match those of conventional quasiperiodic Ising critical points reported before, these fixed points host robust topological edge degeneracies and exhibit a distinct symmetry-enriched realization of the quasiperiodic Ising criticality, as further supported by complementary lattice simulations.

more.abstract: Recently, Mendonça et al. [1] investigated the Dicke-XXZ model and the Dicke-Ising model (DIM) using a variational unitary transformation accompanied by density matrix renormalization group calculations. For the latter model, their calculated quantum phase diagram contradicts claims about the existence of an intermediate antiferromagnetic superradiant phase (AFM-S) and the change in order of some phase transition lines, observed in other studies. In this comment we demonstrate that both features are indeed present in the Dicke-Ising model for the investigated parameter range in Ref. [1].

more.title: Why Ice Is So Slippery
more.abstract: We simulate nanoscale ice-glass friction from first principles and upscale it by modeling frictional heating. Nanoscale simulations alone overestimate friction and miss its velocity dependence. Frictional heating warms the contact toward the melting point, thickening the premelting film tenfold and cutting its viscosity a hundredfold; friction drops with velocity, matching experiment. Premelting forms the film without sliding or heating, but its slipperiness hinges on frictional heating, as Bowden and Hughes proposed in 1939, without melting. Snow, other materials, and coatings remain open.

more.title: Quantized pumping in disordered nonlinear Thouless pumps
more.abstract: We investigate the dynamics of nonlinear optical Thouless pumps in the presence of disorder, using optical waveguide arrays. It was previously known that the displacement of solitons in Thouless pumps is quantized and may exhibit integer and fractional transport over the course of the pump cycle. Here, we demonstrate that, in disordered nonlinear pumps, quantization may be maintained or created through nonlinearity, despite the presence of disorder, even though it would not be in the linear domain. Moreover, nonlinearity allows pumps to be executed more quickly (i.e., less adiabatically). This may serve as a design principle for integrated non-reciprocal devices based on temporal modulation.

more.title: Structural and regulatory evolution across the genus Hordeum
more.abstract: The genus Hordeum comprises cultivated barley and its wild relatives, an evolutionarily, ecologically and agriculturally important group of grasses 1,2 . Here we generated a chromosome-scale comparative genomic resource comprising all recognized diploid Hordeum species together with representative polyploid lineages. Comparative analyses reveal extensive structural variation, including inversions and chromosomal rearrangements that disrupt proximal collinearity and reflect lineage-specific genome remodelling. Single-copy gene phylogenies identify ancient hybridization, segmental exchange and introgression, revealing pervasive reticulate evolution during Hordeum diversification. We uncover widespread horizontal gene transfer from Panicoideae grasses into Hordeum , with many transferred genes showing evidence of transcription and functional integration. Retrotransposon proliferation explains genome size variation and provides insights into polyploid genome evolution. Whole-genome alignments reveal contrasting evolutionary dynamics: whereas coding sequences remain highly conserved, regulatory elements undergo rapid turnover, providing a rich source of regulatory diversity for phenotypic evolution. Case studies of vernalization and glume development demonstrate how natural variation in regulatory and coding sequences contributes to flowering time and floral morphology. This comprehensive pangenomic framework establishes Hordeum as a model for studying genome evolution, structural variation and the genetic basis of adaptive traits, offering new avenues for barley improvement.

more.title: Evidence for late Middle Pleistocene Homo erectus in mainland East Asia
more.abstract: Hominin fossils and genetic evidence indicate that several hominin populations occupied East and Southeast Asia during the Middle and Late Pleistocene epoch1–10. Homo erectus fossils remain scarce in southern China and mainland Southeast Asia4,8,11. Here we report nine newly discovered late Middle Pleistocene hominin teeth from the Naxian and Baxian caves at the Chongzuo study area, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, southern China, dated to around 324–184 thousand years ago12. Palaeoproteomics reveals the presence of an endogenous dental proteome in all five hominin teeth studied molecularly. Four teeth contain a derived H. erectus substitution in ameloblastin that to date has been observed only in older Middle Pleistocene H. erectus specimens from China13. The proteomes of these four teeth differ from the previous H. erectus proteomes from China at another ameloblastin position, suggesting that these specimens represent a previously unsampled H. erectus population. Morphometric and geometric morphometric methods support an attribution of these teeth to H. erectus, as well as four additional teeth. This fills a gap in the geographical and chronological distribution of H. erectus in East Asia. The fifth tooth studied proteomically, PA1796, is morphologically distinct from H. erectus, Neanderthals (Homo neanderthalensis) and modern humans (Homo sapiens), and does not contain the H. erectus-derived amino acid sequence. The late survival of H. erectus on mainland East Asia suggests that at least two hominin lineages, H. erectus and Homo longi (Denisovans)6,7, possibly represented by PA1796, were present in the region towards the end of the Middle Pleistocene, with the first documented occurrence of H. sapiens not much later5. more.title: Rainforest adaptation in late Homo erectus from southern China
more.abstract: Homo erectus represents one of the longest-persisting hominin species, with a geographic range from Africa to eastern Eurasia from approximately 1.9 million years ago 1 to 108 thousand years ago (ka) 2 . Despite this, there are still large gaps in our understanding of the adaptation capabilities of this species and the extent of its persistence in China. Assumptions over ecological preferences based on the Trinil 3 , Sangiran 4 and Ngandong 2 (in Java) open woodland–grassland mosaics have persisted, combined with limited direct stable carbon isotope measurements in Asia. Here we present a rich temporal and environmental context for nine hominin teeth, eight of which were morphologically and genetically identified as H. erectus 5 , found in two sister caves in Guangxi province, southern China. We modelled 43 radiometric ages from five dating techniques to establish a timeline for H. erectus presence in this region. Stable and clumped isotopes and trace elements from teeth were used to establish the dominant environments and their behavioural responses. We show that H. erectus was present in southern China between 324 and 184 ka, which is substantially more recent than previously established in this region for unequivocally H. erectus fossils at approximately 400 ka. The evidence suggests that they were persisting in closed rainforest ecosystems, thought to be the domain of only Homo sapiens , and were demonstrating long-term mobility and ecological flexibility. This evidence challenges the assumptions over the ecological preferences and behavioural limitations of H. erectus .

more.title: PEARLS: NuSTAR and XMM-Newton Extragalactic Survey of the JWST North Ecliptic Pole Time-domain Field V: Unraveling X-Ray Spectral Variability
more.abstract: As one of the first deep time-domain surveys in the hard X-ray band, the NuSTAR campaign in the JWST North Ecliptic Pole Time Domain Field (NEP-TDF) offers a prime opportunity to measure variability in a faint population of active galactic nuclei (AGN) in the medium- to high-redshift Universe. In the X-ray band, AGN variability is generally caused by changes in the brightness of the corona ( F int variability) or changes in the column density of obscuring material near the supermassive black hole (SMBH; N H variability). Broadband spectroscopy (∼0.5–24 keV) is required to reliably disentangle these two phenomena. With simultaneous NuSTAR and XMM-Newton coverage—as well as 1.8 Ms of Chandra monitoring—the X-ray surveys in the NEP-TDF are ideally situated for this purpose. This work presents the first spectral modeling of the 52 NuSTAR-identified sources discovered in the latter half of the campaign, as well as a spectroscopic variability study of the entire 112-source NuSTAR NEP-TDF catalog. Seven variable candidates are identified. We find that ≳1000 total counts split across many (≳10) epochs are needed in order to detect variability. Additionally, variable sources are compared to the survey sensitivity in order to inform population synthesis models of how variations can affect the detectability of faint AGN, which dominate the SMBH accretion history. Lastly, the timescale of N H variability is investigated as a probe for the obscurer location. Significant variability is slightly more common on >100 day timescales, suggesting that the torus may have only slight dominance in driving N H variability in faint AGN.

more.title: Tracing Radial Structures of Molecular Gas and Gas-phase Metallicity across the Galaxy Merger Sequence with KILOGAS
more.abstract: Galaxy interactions and mergers are expected to redistribute baryons across galactic disks, yet how molecular gas and metals are reorganized as a function of merger stage remains unclear. In this work, we investigate the radial structure of molecular gas and gas-phase metallicity (oxygen abundance traced by O3N2 ) using a large sample of nearby galaxies from the Kiloparsec Investigations of Local Objects’ Gas And Star formation (KILOGAS) survey spanning a wide range of interaction stages. We construct galaxy-by-galaxy radial profiles of molecular gas surface density and metallicity and characterize their shapes. We find that a significant fraction of gas-rich, star-forming galaxies, regardless of merger stage, deviates from simple single-slope profiles, and that molecular gas and metallicity do not always evolve in a coupled manner. The inner molecular gas profiles become progressively steeper along the merger sequence relative to matched control galaxies, with the strongest deviations observed in postmerger systems. The outer profiles, meanwhile, become flatter, consistent with merger-driven inflows redistributing gas toward the center. Metallicity profiles also tend to steepen with advancing merger stage, particularly in the inner regions, while exhibiting no systematic change in the outer regions relative to control galaxies. This weaker and more spatially limited metallicity response likely reflects the combined effects of gas inflow, chemical enrichment, and mixing, which operate on different timescales and can partially offset one another. Overall, our results establish radial profile shapes as a powerful diagnostic of baryon redistribution in galaxy interactions.

more.title: Directed Attachment of Catalysts into the Extended Environments of Soft Photoelectrodes for Hydrogen Evolution
more.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
more.abstract: We present a detailed investigation of early stage photoelectrochemical deposition of platinum nanoparticle (Pt-NP) catalysts on semiconducting polymer platforms for the light-assisted hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) using electrochemical, spectroscopic, and microscopy characterization, combined with density functional theory (DFT) modeling. The photoactive junction─formed from a blend of donor (PTB7-Th) and acceptor (P(NDI2OD-T2)) polymers─exhibits HER efficiencies that increase exponentially with Pt-NP loading (ca. 8.0 × 101 to 2.5 × 104 ng/cm2) of highly faceted Pt-NPs. The blended heterojunction demonstrates acceptor enrichment of the near-surface region as the point of Pt deposition via progressive nucleation, at sites which we posit are the near-surface termini of “fast transport pathways” created within the PTB7-Th/P(NDI2OD-T2) blend film. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), for the lowest coverage Pt-NPs, combined with DFT modeling, suggests Pt–S interactions via the bithiophene groups in P(NDI2OD-T2) might dominate at the earliest stages of Pt deposition, while larger DFT-modeled 14- and 38-atom Pt clusters demonstrate Pt–C and Pt–O═C interactions on naphthalene diimide cores. Collectively, our findings suggest that submicron environments in soft photoelectrode materials function as integrated architectures, as expected, where charge creation requires well mixed domains, adjacent to domains optimized for charge transport. Photoelectrochemically deposited metals such as Pt-NPs decorate the most photoelectrochemically active near-surface regions, producing good HER efficiencies. Hierarchical assembly of such photoactive soft materials has the potential to provide a transformative framework for scalable energy conversion that extends beyond hydrogen…

more.title: Unveiling the Dark Matter Nature with Reionization Relics
more.abstract: Dark matter constitutes roughly one-fourth of the Universe, yet its physical nature remains unknown. Warm dark matter (WDM), a class of dark matter candidates, has nonnegligible velocity dispersion that suppresses the formation of small-scale cosmic structures. Current constraints therefore rely mainly on small-scale probes such as the Ly α forest and Milky Way observations of satellite galaxies and stellar streams. We propose a novel large-scale probe based on long-lived “reionization relics”: because the thermal and dynamical evolution of the intergalactic medium depends on the local reionization redshift, patchy reionization imprints additional large-scale fluctuations in Ly α forest opacity and post-reionization H I traced by 21 cm intensity mapping. The strength of these imprints depends on WDM through both small-scale gas evolution and WDM-driven changes in the reionization history. For example, the Ly α (21 cm) power spectrum in 3 keV WDM differs from cold dark matter by ≃19% (≃19%) at k = 0.05 Mpc −1 at z = 4 ( z = 5.5) when reionization relics are included. Using Ly α forest with a covariance model designed to mimic the capabilities of the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI), we forecast a constraint of m WDM > 5.0 keV (95%), which improves to m WDM > 7.1 keV when combined with 21 cm intensity-mapping observations from the Square Kilometre Array (SKA). The next-generation surveys can further strengthen the current best lower bounds from 9.7 to 39 keV.

more.title: Divergent activation of the RXFP1 relaxin receptor by protein and small-molecule agonists
more.abstract: The relaxin receptor RXFP1 is a therapeutic target owing to its potential benefits in the treatment of fibrosis and heart failure. Protein and small-molecule agonists are currently in midstage clinical trials for various forms of heart disease. In this work, we present three cryo–electron microscopy structures of RXFP1: ligand-free, bound to the native agonist relaxin-2, and bound to the small-molecule drug candidate AZD5462. These structures reveal that relaxin-2 engages the receptor’s ectodomain, whereas AZD5462 binds to the transmembrane domain. Together with hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry, we show that relaxin-2 induces reorganization of the linker domain into a helical secondary structure. By contrast, AZD5462 stabilizes an active conformation through a distinct set of conformational rearrangements. Altogether, our findings define divergent activation mechanisms for protein and small-molecule agonists of RXFP1.

more.title: Unemployment Benefits and Unemployment in the Great Recession: The Role of Equilibrium Effects
more.abstract: Equilibrium labor market theory suggests that unemployment benefit extensions affect unemployment by impacting both job search decisions by the unemployed and job creation decisions by employers. The existing empirical literature focused on the former effect only. We develop a new methodology necessary to incorporate the measurement of the latter effect. Implementing this methodology in the data, we find that benefit extensions raise equilibrium wages and lead to a sharp contraction in vacancy creation and employment and a rise in unemployment.
more.topic: Labor market dynamics and wage inequality

more.title: Enhanced Multiphase Circumgalactic Medium and Gas Cycling in Galaxy Mergers
more.abstract: We investigate the impact of galaxy mergers on the circumgalactic medium (CGM) using the FIREbox cosmological hydrodynamic simulation. By comparing matched samples of merging and isolated galaxies with stellar masses M ⋆ ∼ 10 10 –10 11 M ⊙ at z = 0 and merger mass ratios larger than 1: 10, we find that mergers significantly alter CGM properties. Merging systems exhibit enhanced radiative cooling, leading to shorter cooling times than free–fall times across large CGM volumes. This results in amplified multiphase structure and increased cool/cold gas content ( T ∼ 10 4 K) compared to isolated galaxies. Both inflow and outflow mass fluxes are elevated across a wide range, and the enhancement is mostly pronounced in cool (∼10 4 K) and hot (∼10 6 K) phases by at least ∼1 dex in mergers, with cool gas primarily generated in situ via radiative cooling rather than from pre-existing streams. Gas cycling analysis reveals that mergers fundamentally accelerate CGM processing, amplifying the effective transfer rate from cold/cool cosmic inflow to galaxy inflow by factors of ∼27 through rapid cycling of inflowing gas through intermediate CGM phases, efficiently fueling the interstellar medium and star formation. The enhanced cool gas content in mergers produces elevated column densities for low- and intermediate-temperature ion species in the inner CGM, while high-temperature species remain largely unaffected.

more.title: Conservation of the tumour microenvironment across organs and species
more.abstract: Current understanding of the host tissue response to solid tumours is largely based on investigations of tumour types in isolation 1 . Given the breadth and diversity of human tumour pathology and contributions of tumour microenvironment (TME) cells to disease progression, pan-cancer analysis is needed to bridge major themes of stromal and immune cell evolution. To date, however, efforts to compare the TME response across cancers have been limited in scope 2 , 3 . Here we conduct a comprehensive pan-cancer analysis by algorithmically screening thousands of publicly available single-cell transcriptomic datasets for stromal and immune signatures across species and tissue types. We demonstrate conserved hallmarks of host cell transcriptional programming in response to malignancy across 42 cancer types in more than 2,000 human and mouse tumour samples. These findings are codified as an interactive web atlas ( tmeatlas.stanford.edu ) and software package (scTME) that will serve as practical resources for the systematic interrogation of the TME in tumours.

more.title: 8-Oxoguanine Is the Major Product of the Reaction of Guanine Radical Cations with •NO2: A Spin-Orchestrated, Anisotropic Reaction Landscape and Its Biological Implications
more.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
more.abstract: Formation of guanine radical cations (G•+) represents a hallmark DNA lesion produced by ionizing radiation and one-electron oxidation processes. •NO2, a reactive nitrogen species in living systems, drives nitrative and oxidative damage linked to mutagenesis and inflammation. Herein, we delineate spin-orchestrated interactions between •NO2 and radical cations of 2′-deoxyguanosine (dGuo•+) and its model compound 9-methylguanine (9MG•+) to probe synergistic pathways that exacerbate guanine nucleobase and nucleoside damage. Kinetic energy-resolved reaction coupled with mass spectrometric measurements revealed distinct pathways governing regioselective nitrite- and nitro-additions, adduct decomposition, and charge transfer. Direct dynamics simulations and potential energy surface analyses of the 9MG•+ + •NO2 model system, using spin-projected and time-dependent DFT, CCSD(T), and CASPT2 theories, characterized reaction mechanisms, thermodynamics, and kinetics arising from anisotropic interactions within open-shell 1,OS[G•+(↑)···(↓)•NO2] and 3[G•+(↑)···(↑)•NO2]. Through radical combination, the reaction system advances through multiple excited electronic and vibrational manifolds while preserving spin states (no intersystem crossing); only singlet states are open to chemical transformations. •NO2 markedly amplifies the lesion of guanine radicals by promoting sequential electron and H loss, producing 8-oxoguanine in neutral, radical cation, and doubly oxidized forms, along with release of •NO, NO+, and HNO. These pathways proceed through nitrite addition rather than guanine nitration, and HNO forms through •NO-mediated hydrogen abstraction via both conventional and roaming mechanisms. The studies identified new routes to the 8-oxoguanine lesion that has been traditionally…

more.title: Development and Application of Nanopore Direct RNA Sequencing
more.abstract: Individual RNA strands can be sequenced directly using nanoscale protein pores. This process, Nanopore Direct RNA Sequencing (Nanopore DRS), uses a helicase motor protein to regulate RNA displacement through the nanopore orifice in single nucleotide steps. Partial blockade of the monovalent ionic current is recorded at 4 kHz and converted to a string of RNA nucleotide basecalls using machine learning models. In this review, we discuss the development of Nanopore DRS from 1996 to the present. This includes performance metrics, evolution of machine learning models, and applications of Nanopore DRS to major RNA classes across kingdoms. Advantages of the technology are highlighted with special emphasis on nucleotide modifications along intact single strands. Shortcomings of the technology are also considered along with possible solutions. We close with forward looking Nanopore DRS applications: Single cell RNA sequencing; remote monitoring of infectious agents; principled understanding of nanopore ionic current patterns using all-atoms simulations; global food security; and clinical applications.

more.title: Assessing Multiple Treatment Regimens for Tuberculosis
more.abstract: MethodsIn this phase 2, randomized, controlled trial, we assigned participants with rifampin-susceptible pulmonary tuberculosis to receive the standard four-drug combination (isoniazid–rifampin–pyrazinamide–ethambutol; HRZE) for 24 weeks; bedaquiline–delamanid–moxifloxacin for 16 weeks; or one of 10 new four-drug combinations for 16 weeks. The new regimens contained ganfeborole, BTZ-043, or both, with combinations of bedaquiline, delamanid, moxifloxacin, pyrazinamide, pretomanid, and linezolid. The primary end point was the log10(time to positivity) slope (rate of change from baseline to week 12 in the time to Mycobacterium tuberculosis growth in a positive sputum culture). The treatment effect was assessed as the Bayesian posterior probability of superiority of each new regimen to HRZE with respect to the primary end point (results were used to select regimens for further evaluation, rather than for characterization of efficacy). ResultsA total of 401 participants underwent randomization; 371 were included in the modified intention-to-treat population and 400 in the safety population. We identified two promising regimens for further evaluation: ganfeborole–bedaquiline–pretomanid–moxifloxacin (BPMG) and BTZ-043–bedaquiline–delamanid–moxifloxacin (BDMT). The log10(time to positivity) slope was 0.129 log10(days) per week (95% Bayesian credible interval, 0.112 to 0.146) with BPMG and 0.142 log10(days) per week (95% Bayesian credible interval, 0.126 to 0.160) with BDMT, as compared with 0.118 log10(days) per week (95% Bayesian credible interval, 0.105 to 0.131) with HRZE, for a relative difference of 9.1% (95% Bayesian credible interval, −8.6 to 29.0) and 20.5% (95% Bayesian credible interval, 2.7 to 41.1), respectively, and a posterior probability of superiority of 0.83…

more.title: Balancing redox-mediated cytotoxicity and catalysis in natural product biosynthesis
more.abstract: Redox-mediated chemistry is central to both the biosynthesis and cytotoxicity of many natural products, yet how microbes balance these processes remains poorly understood. Here, we uncover a conserved mechanism that coordinates three redox-mediated processes in secondary metabolite biosynthesis: self-protection, prevention of substrate degradation, and late-stage biosynthesis. Using the antitumor antibiotic doxorubicin as a model system, we show that the vicinal oxygen chelate (VOC) protein DnrV prevents reactive oxygen species formation and substrate degradation while promoting P450 catalysis. We expand this paradigm to a conserved family of VOC-fold proteins, redox-associated cytotoxin-binding proteins (REACT), found across bacteria, fungi, and plants. REACT represents a multifunctional protein class that balances antibiotic assembly, self-protection, and prevention of metabolite destruction, providing a foundational understanding of production of redox-active natural products.

more.title: Telemetric calorimetry for wireless continuous reaction profiling
more.abstract: Real-time monitoring of chemical reactions is often achieved with specialized instrumentation along with custom-designed reactors or intrusive sampling. In this study, we introduce reaction telemetry, a wireless analytical strategy that enables remote, nonintrusive monitoring directly within operating reaction vessels. This approach uses light-powered microelectronic devices that communicate optically and function as autonomous sensing elements. We demonstrate continuous calorimetric measurements across diverse chemical reactions relevant to pharmaceutical and fine chemical synthesis, including photochemical and electrochemical systems, providing access to reaction kinetics under native operating conditions with subsecond temporal resolution. The resulting measurements will support catalyst evaluation, safety assessment, and mechanistic investigation and will accelerate data-driven reaction discovery. By embedding analytical functionality directly within reaction vessels, reaction telemetry establishes a general framework for information-rich observation of chemical processes across research, development, and education.

more.title: Molecular Origins of Lithium-Ion Transport in the Anionic Metal–Organic Framework SU-102
more.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
more.abstract: Metal–organic framework (MOF) quasi-solid electrolytes offer chemically tunable environments for ion transport, but the molecular roles of framework coordination and confined solvent remain unclear. We combined solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (ssNMR) measurements with molecular dynamics simulations to determine the Li+ transport mechanism in propylene carbonate (PC)-filled SU-102. Variable-temperature direct- and cross-polarization 7Li ssNMR reveal two distinct Li+ populations with different local tumbling dynamics. Our simulations identified Zr-associated, linker-associated, and fully PC-solvated Li+ coordination environments. The most strongly stabilizing Li+ site is not necessarily the one that carries transport: Zr-associated sites bind Li+ most strongly but form a discontinuous network along the pore axis, whereas the weaker-binding linker sites form a continuous one. Linker-associated Li+ also shows faster site-persistence decay and the largest trial-weighted displacement, and linker-to-linker hopping is the most frequent classified event, followed by Zr-to-Zr hopping. Chemical color-diffusion nonequilibrium molecular dynamics yielded an ionic conductivity of 1.34 ± 0.48 mS cm–1 along the one-dimensional channels and negligible conductivity perpendicular to them, giving an orientational average of 0.45 ± 0.16 mS cm–1, in close agreement with experiment (0.52 mS cm–1). Together, our results indicate that PC-assisted hopping between linker sites contributes more strongly than vehicular diffusion of fully solvated ions, with confined PC retained in the coordination shell across these transfers. These findings identify the balance between ion–framework stabilization and facile site-to-site exchange as a key design principle for reticular quasi-solid…

more.title: A thalamo-amygdalar circuit drives female vulnerability to chronic pain after early-life stress
more.abstract: Childhood adversity increases the risk of chronic pain and anxiety later in life, particularly in women, yet the neural mechanisms linking early-life stress to adult vulnerability remain elusive. Here, we show that social isolation and nerve injury interact to amplify activity-dependent synaptic gain and anticipatory recruitment of the paraventricular thalamus-to–central amygdala pathway in female, but not male, mice. This female-specific circuit sensitization enhances mechanical hypersensitivity and avoidance behaviors in adulthood. Chemogenetic pathway inhibition selectively rescued these behaviors when stress and injury co-occurred, whereas sustained and phasic pathway activation triggered mechanical hypersensitivity and avoidance, respectively. Together, these findings uncovered a latent thalamo-amygdalar synaptic gain state that is unmasked by a subsequent injury and transforms early-life stress into female-specific vulnerability to chronic pain and anxiety-like avoidance.

more.title: Stereochemical Identity of a Single Fluorosugar Enables Noninvasive Dual-Biomarker Fingerprinting of Cancer
more.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
more.abstract: Clinical molecular imaging of cancer largely relies on single biomarker-attributable readouts. Through an efficient trapping mechanism, 2-[18F]FDG robustly links PET readouts to the Warburg effect, illuminating only a single metabolic axis within the multichannel biochemical network of cancer. The versatile chemical space of synthetic fluorosugars, however, may offer an attractive framework for broadening the repertoire of metabolic markers accessible to noninvasive imaging. Here, we report Fluorine Metabolic Imaging (FMI), a molecular MRI strategy for simultaneous in vivo mapping of two metabolic biomarkers using a single probe. FMI exploits the altered biochemistry of 3-fluoro-3-deoxy-d-galactose (3FDGal), which undergoes orthogonal intracellular redox transformations mediated by ALDH1A1 and AKR1B1, each yielding a stably trapped fluorine-labeled metabolite with a characteristic 19F-NMR peak. Concurrently mapped by 19F-MRI, these two enzyme-attributable readouts enable noninvasive spatially resolved dual-biomarker visualization. We establish the trapping mechanism of 3FDGal and its enzymatic basis, demonstrating that 3FDGal-initiated fingerprints reflect dual-biomarker variations across different cancer cells. In vivo, FMI distinguishes tumors with contrasting metabolic phenotypes, herein demonstrated in human xenografts not detectable by the canonical 2-[18F]FDG-PET approach. Establishing this proof-of-concept platform for noninvasive multilayered tumor subtyping, FMI with fluorosugars extends metabolic imaging beyond the Warburg scheme into unexplored dimensions of cancer diagnostics.

more.title: Equity in Maternal–Fetal Medicine — Technological Advances and a Potential Path Forward
more.abstract: Without safeguards, rapid technological development in maternal–fetal medicine could reinforce existing racial, socioeconomic, and geographic inequities in prenatal care.

more.title: Substitution Reactions of Halogen-Substituted Acetals: Glycosylations and Related Reactions
more.abstract: The nucleophilic substitution reactions of halogen-substituted acetals are useful for the synthesis of a variety of compounds, most particularly of sugar derivatives. This review will summarize the current understanding of the mechanisms involved in these reactions and will present substitution reactions of carbohydrate derivatives with fluorine, chlorine, bromine, and iodine substituents. The halogen atom at C-2 can have a powerful influence on the stereoselectivities of the glycosylation reactions, most often leading to 1,2-trans stereoselectivity. Examples of the uses of these halogen-substituted products will also be provided.

more.title: Diffusion Models for Small-Molecule Design
more.abstract: Diffusion models (DMs) have emerged as a class of generative models for controllable small-molecule design in drug discovery capable of progressively transforming noisy or partially specified molecular states into candidate structures under structural, geometric, and property constraints. This Review provides a comprehensive overview of the methodological foundations and representative applications of diffusion-based molecular generation, emphasizing the alignment among molecular representations, generative dynamics, controllable design, and evaluation and validation. Particular attention is given to recent advances in property- and structure-guided generation, target-aware and fragment-based design, multiobjective optimization, and synthesis-aware generation. We also discuss the roles of data sets, computational evaluation, and prospective experiments in assessing the chemical and biological relevance of generated molecules. By organizing these developments within a unified conceptual framework, we provide computational chemists and drug discovery researchers with a structured roadmap that balances the mathematical rigor with chemical intuition. Throughout, we highlight current methodological limitations and unresolved challenges and conclude with future directions toward chemically credible and experimentally grounded molecular design. To facilitate navigation of this rapidly evolving field, we introduce an interactive companion platform (https://diffsmd.scbdd.com) that provides a curated, continuously updated repository of model architectures and visualizations.

more.title: Transition metal-catalyzed carborane cage B–H activation and functionalization: a mechanistic view
more.abstract: B-H activation affects the energy level of further functionalization, and thus the selectivity is determined by B-H activation or subsequent functionalization. Therefore, the factors dictating selectivity can be identified by analyzing the transition state properties, providing insights into improving regio- or chiral-at-cage selectivities. The opportunities and challenges for future research are discussed. We highlight strategies of exploiting the unique characteristics of carboranes based on C-H bond activation protocols and single-electron transfer approaches including photo- and electrocatalysis. We expect that this review will provide a framework for understanding the catalytic mechanism, rational catalyst design, and exploration of precise functionalization strategies.

more.title: Fault-Tolerant Execution of Error-Corrected Quantum Algorithms
more.abstract: Scaling up quantum algorithms to tackle high-impact problems in science and industry requires quantum error correction and fault tolerance. While progress has been made in experimentally realizing error-corrected primitives, the end-to-end execution of logical quantum algorithms using only fault-tolerant (FT) components has remained out of reach. We demonstrate the FT and error-corrected execution of two quantum algorithms, the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) and the Harrow-Hassidim-Lloyd algorithm applied to the Poisson equation, on Quantinuum H2 and Helios trapped-ion quantum processors using the ⟦ 7 , 1 , 3 ⟧ Steane code. For QAOA circuits on five and six logical qubits, we show performance improvements from increasing the number of QAOA layers and the number of T gates used to approximate logical rotations, despite increased physical circuit complexity. We further show that QAOA circuits with up to eight logical qubits and nine logical T gates perform similarly to unencoded circuits. For the largest QAOA circuits we run, with 12 logical (97 physical) qubits and 2132 physical two-qubit gates, we still observe better-than-random performance. Finally, we show that adding active quantum error correction cycles and increasing the repeat-until-success limit of state-preparation subroutines can improve the performance of a quantum algorithm, thereby demonstrating critical capabilities of scalable FT quantum computation. Our results are enabled by a FT logical T -gate implementation with an infidelity of 2.7 ( 4 ) × 10 − 3 and dynamic circuits with measurement-dependent feedback. Our work demonstrates near-breakeven performance of complex, error-corrected algorithmic quantum circuits using only FT components.

more.title: Revertant Autograft Replacement in Recessive Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa
more.abstract: Two adolescents with epidermolysis bullosa received autografts from revertant skin, which provided durable epidermal replacement over approximately 95% of the body-surface area in one patient and 50% in the other.

more.title: Redox metabolism at the host–pathogen interface in Mycobacterium tuberculosis
more.abstract: Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) persists within the host despite robust immune responses and prolonged multidrug therapy, underscoring the need to better understand the mechanisms that drive persistence and treatment failure. Emerging evidence indicates that redox metabolism is a central interface governing host-pathogen interactions during tuberculosis (TB). This review discusses how redox cross talk integrates immune signaling with bacterial physiology through interconnected pathways involving iron metabolism, lipid peroxidation, mitochondrial bioenergetics, central carbon metabolism, and antioxidant defenses. We highlight how these processes generate physiological, metabolic, and spatial heterogeneity within infected macrophages and granulomas, promoting bacterial persistence, drug tolerance, and tissue pathology. Finally, we discuss therapeutic strategies targeting redox-dependent vulnerabilities in both the host and the pathogen, including modulation of macrophage bioenergetics, nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2) signaling, ferroptosis, and mycobacterial respiration. Integrating host and bacterial redox biology provides a unified framework for developing host-directed and pathogen-directed interventions to improve TB treatment and limit long-term disease sequelae.

more.title: Rising Wages and the Decline of Low-Wage Work
more.abstract: From 2014 to 2024, the share of U.S. hourly workers paid below $15 in real terms fell by two-thirds, from 38 percent to 13 percent. Why? We first distinguish the entry and exit of employers—wherein high-paying employers have supplanted low-paying ones—from organizational changes among incumbent employers. Organizational changes can be imposed on employers by external constraints, like labor market tightness, or emerge from the pursuit of new opportunities. Using panel data drawn from administrative records and job reviews, we bring this framework to bear on the recent wage gains at the bottom of the labor market. Contrary to predictions of creative destruction, we can trace only a small amount of these wage gains to the disappearance of low-wage organizations. Instead, the main driver of rising pay was low- and middle-paying incumbent employers of low-wage occupations increasing pay. These gains in low-wage occupations were associated with tightening labor markets and increased minimum wages. But over and above these external constraints, employers also pursued new opportunities for reorganizing work in low-skill jobs. Notwithstanding organizational inertia, major gains for workers’ pay can come from changes in existing workplaces.
more.topic: Labor market dynamics and wage inequality

more.title: Noninvertible Bosonic Chiral Symmetry on the Lattice
more.abstract: In this work, we realize the 3 + 1 D noninvertible Z N chiral symmetry generator as an operator in a many-body lattice Hilbert space. A crucial ingredient in our construction is the use of infinite-dimensional U(1) rotor site Hilbert spaces. Specifically, our Hilbert space is that of a U(1) lattice gauge theory coupled to a charge 1 scalar in the Villain formulation, which allows for direct access to monopoles and for a simple definition of a magnetic Z N one-form symmetry Z m ( 1 ) , at the lattice Hamiltonian level. We construct the generator of the Z N chiral symmetry as a locality-preserving unitary operator not in the entire Hilbert space but only in the subspace of Z m ( 1 ) -invariant states. Using a lattice-level duality based on gauging Z m ( 1 ) , we find a dual description of this subspace, as the subspace of a charge 1 / N gauge theory invariant under an electric one-form symmetry Z e ( 1 ) . We show that, in this dual formulation, the chiral symmetry generator extends unitarily to the entire Hilbert space but has a mixed anomaly with the Z e ( 1 ) symmetry.

more.title: Realization of a Cavity-Coupled Rydberg Array
more.abstract: Scalable quantum computers and quantum networks require the combination of quantum processing nodes with efficient light-matter interfaces to distribute quantum information in local or long-distance quantum networks. Neutral-atom arrays have both been coupled to Rydberg states to enable high-fidelity quantum gates in universal processing architectures, and to optical cavities to realize interfaces to photons. However, combining these two capabilities and coupling atom arrays to highly excited Rydberg states in the mode of an optical cavity has been an outstanding challenge. Here we present a novel cavity-coupled Rydberg array that achieves this long-standing goal. We prepare, detect, and control individual atoms in a scalable optical tweezer array, couple them strongly to the optical mode of a high-finesse optical cavity and excite them in a controlled way to Rydberg states. We show that high-cooperativity coupling to an optical cavity—demonstrated via the dispersive shift of the resonance of the cavity in presence of the atoms—and strong Rydberg interactions—demonstrated via the collective enhancement of Rydberg coupling in the atomic array—can be achieved in our setup at the same spatial location. Our presented experimental platform opens the path to several new directions, including the realization of quantum network nodes, quantum simulation of long-range interacting, open quantum systems, and photonic-state engineering leveraging high-fidelity Rydberg control.

more.title: Market Response to Racial Uprisings
more.abstract: Do investors anticipate that demands for racial equity will impact companies? We explore this question in the context of the Black Lives Matter (BLM) movement—the largest racially motivated protest movement in U.S. history—and its effect on the U.S. policing industry using a novel dataset on publicly traded firms contracting with the police. It is unclear whether the BLM uprisings were likely to increase or decrease market valuations of firms contracting heavily with police because of the increased interest in reforming the police, fears over rising crime, and pushes to “defund the police”. We find, in contrast to the predictions of economics experts we surveyed, that in the three weeks following incidents triggering BLM uprisings, policing firms experienced a stock price increase of seven percentage points relative to the stock prices of nonpolicing firms in similar industries. In particular, firms producing surveillance technology and police accountability tools experienced higher returns following BLM activism–related events. Furthermore, policing firms’ fundamentals, such as sales, improved after the murder of George Floyd, suggesting that policing firms’ future performances bore out investors' positive expectations following incidents triggering BLM uprisings. Our research shows how—despite BLM’s calls to reduce investment in policing and explore alternative public safety approaches—the financial market has translated high-profile violence against Black civilians and calls for systemic change into shareholder gains and additional revenues for police suppliers.

more.title: Case 33-2026: A 73-Year-Old Woman with Fever, Weight Loss, and Leg Weakness
more.abstract: A 73-year-old woman presented with fever, weight loss, and leg weakness. A chest radiograph showed biapical pleural and parenchymal scarring and diffuse reticular opacities. A diagnosis was made.

more.title: Realization of Repulsive Polarons in the Strongly Correlated Regime
more.abstract: Mobile impurities interacting with a quantum medium form quasiparticles known as polarons, a central concept in many-body physics. While the quantum impurity problem has been extensively studied with ultracold atomic gases, repulsive polarons in the strongly correlated regime have remained elusive. Typically, the impurity atoms bind into molecules or rapidly decay into deeper-lying states before they can acquire an appreciable dressing cloud. Here, we report on the realization of polarons in a strongly repulsive two-dimensional quantum gas. Using a superfluid of Li 6 dimers, we introduce impurities by promoting a small fraction of the dimers into higher levels of the transverse confining potential. These novel synthetic-spin polarons give access to the strongly repulsive regime where common decay channels are suppressed. We extract key polaron properties—the energy, quasiparticle residue, and effective mass—using trap modulation and Bragg spectroscopy. Our measurements are well captured by a microscopic T -matrix approach and quantum Monte Carlo simulations, revealing deviations from mean-field predictions. In particular, we measure a significant enhancement of the polaron mass, with values exceeding twice the free-dimer mass. Our demonstration of a stable repulsive Bose polaron establishes a platform for studying impurity physics in low-dimensional and strongly correlated systems.

more.title: The 2MIG isolated AGNs – 3. Optical–IR variability and dust reverberation in the NLSy1 galaxies Mrk 42 and Mrk 493
more.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
more.abstract: We present an optical–infrared variability study of two isolated narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies, Mrk 42 and Mrk 493, using ZTF optical and WISE/NEOWISE W1/W2 light curves, supplemented by ATLAS, SDSS, Swift, and IAC80 data. We analyse colour–magnitude and flux–flux relations and measure optical–infrared reverberation lags using flux-randomisation and random-subset-selection (FR/RSS) realisations of the interpolated cross-correlation function after correcting the WISE light curves for the variable accretion-disc contribution. For Mrk 42, we obtain observed-frame lags of 54⁺¹³₋₃₃ and 62⁺⁷₋₃₅ d in W1 and W2, respectively. After applying the redshift/wavelength correction, these correspond to dust-response radii of 0.045^(+0.011)_(-0.028) and 0.052^(+0.006)_(-0.029) pc. For Mrk 493, the corresponding observed-frame lags are 94⁺¹⁸₋₂₁ and 111⁺²⁶₋₂₄ d, giving corrected dust-response radii of 0.078^(+0.015)_(-0.017) and 0.092^(+0.021)_(-0.020) pc, respectively. Both galaxies show optical bluer-when-brighter behaviour, whereas their W1 − W2 responses differ: the relation is significant in Mrk 493 but not in Mrk 42, where host and circumnuclear dilution may be stronger. For Mrk 42, SDSS spectral decomposition provides a host-corrected active galactic nucleus (AGN) luminosity for the contextual broad-line region (BLR) comparison. The measured dust-response radii are broadly consistent with the low-luminosity extension and intrinsic scatter of published Rdust–Lbol relations. The major optical flare in Mrk 42 exhibits four broad internal maxima with an intra-flare timescale of approximately 45–47 d; non-uniform peak intervals and stochastic-model comparisons favour flare substructure within a broader accretion-driven event. more.title: Optimizing phenotype scale improves genetic analyses in large-scale biobanks
more.abstract: Large-scale biobanks have enabled increasingly complicated genetic analyses across thousands of phenotypes. However, studies rarely consider the appropriateness of the phenotype scale, which can drastically affect inference on genetic architecture. Here we introduce SIQReg, which learns a data-driven phenotype scale by minimizing heterogeneity across phenotype quantiles. Across 25 UK Biobank complex traits, SIQReg rejects the default scale for 24. Generally, SIQReg scales lie between default and logarithmic, indicating that traits are neither purely additive nor purely multiplicative. SIQReg improves both nonadditive and additive genetic analyses. It eliminates most nonadditive signals, including 97% of variance quantitative trait loci, indicating that they may be scale-induced, while preserving biologically plausible nonadditive signals. It simultaneously improves power for additive signals, increasing identification of genome-wide association loci and transcriptome-wide association genes by 11% and 13%, respectively, improving polygenic prediction accuracy by 10%, and identifying 50% more high-risk individuals. These gains are replicated across ancestry groups. Our results establish SIQReg as a principled phenotype scale transformation approach that improves genetic analyses of complex traits.

more.title: Dust Formation in Common Envelope Binary Interactions — III. Lightcurves
more.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
more.abstract: Luminous red novae are transient events thought to arise from common envelope binary interactions. In this paper, we perform post-processing light-curve calculations for two, 3D hydrodynamic simulations of common envelope events between 1.7 M⊙ and 3.7 M⊙ asymptotic giant branch stars and a 0.6 M⊙ compact companion, simulated for 44 years under adiabatic conditions, with dust nucleation included. In both our simulations, we observe a bright, hot peak lasting 3–5 years, primarily due to photospheric expansion before and during inspiral. Additional peaks appear for different viewing angles due to the interaction’s asymmetry. Dust forms about 1–3 years after the beginning of the simulated interaction, and shortly afterwards, followed by a partial recovery and a plateau with a colour temperature of ~400 K. The dust photosphere reaches a size of ~250 au by the end of the simulations, but would become optically thin at visible wavelengths in 2000–6000 years, revealing an inner, warmer photosphere. Our results are most reliable around the time of peak and the immediate light decline; outside this window, they remain largely qualitative due to two well-quantified but substantial uncertainties—insufficient surface resolution in the first 1–2 years and the adiabatic assumption in the later years. We finally contextualise our simulations within a group of observed luminous red nova transients, drawing particular attention to the outburst of OGLE-2002-BLG-360 and AT 2025abao, which are the only two luminous red novae to date understood to be the interaction of a companion with low-to-intermediate-mass giant stars.

more.title: Intermediate Input Prices and the Labor Share
more.abstract: We argue that the relative price of materials is an important determinant of the labor share of income. When materials and primary inputs are complements and the profit share is positive, a higher price of materials lowers the labor share and raises the profit share of value added, without requiring markups or returns to scale to change. We show that materials-price fluctuations align with U.S. labor-share trends, provide causal evidence on this mechanism across industries and commuting zones, and quantify its importance in a dynamic quantitative model. Finally, we use our mechanism to rationalize differential labor-share trends across countries. Institutional subscribers to the NBER working paper series, and residents of developing countries may download this paper without additional charge at www.nber.org.

shortlist.title: Four-Loop Nonsinglet Splitting Functions in QCD
shortlist.abstract: The scale evolution of parton distributions is governed by splitting functions. We compute the four-loop splitting functions in perturbative QCD that control the evolution of quark nonsinglet distributions. We confirm previous partial results and obtain, for the first time, fully analytic expressions for all nonsinglet contributions at this order. These allow us to extract the analytic form of the four-loop virtual and rapidity anomalous dimensions entering logarithmic resummation. We provide precise numerical representations of the splitting functions suitable for parton evolution.

shortlist.title: Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome
shortlist.abstract: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is a common cause of acute hypoxemic respiratory failure in patients with pneumonia, sepsis, aspiration of gastric contents, severe trauma, or other inciting triggers. Although the definition of the syndrome has evolved over the past several decades, the core elements (acute onset, hypoxemia, and bilateral radiographic opacities) remain consistent. Critical components of management include identification and treatment of the underlying cause of ARDS as well as avoidance of ventilator-induced lung injury and volume overload. Ongoing areas of controversy include the best strategy for supporting nonintubated patients, personalization of positive end-expiratory pressure, the role of innovative ventilatory strategies, and the use of glucocorticoids. New research suggests that precision medicine approaches to ARDS management that focus on discrete biologic, radiographic, or physiological subphenotypes may improve outcomes, and prospective trials of these approaches are ongoing.

shortlist.title: Quantum-classical separation in bounded-resource tasks arising from measurement contextuality
shortlist.abstract: Quantum phenomena can be exploited to tackle certain problems beyond the reach of classical approaches. In this study, we focus on coordinated decision-making among many players without communication, the study of which, on current quantum processors, has remained elusive. Using a superconducting qubit processor, we show that quantum contextuality enables certain tasks to be performed with success probabilities beyond classical limits. With a few qubits, we illustrate quantum contextuality with the magic square game and quantify it through a Bell-Kochen-Specker inequality violation. To examine many-body contextuality, we implement the N -player Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger game and separately solve a two-dimensional hidden linear function problem, advancing the state of the art on fidelity and system size in both tasks. Our work introduces benchmarking of quantum processors using contextuality-based algorithms.

shortlist.title: Zero-shot de novo design of a metalloenzyme
shortlist.abstract: De novo design of enzymes is a frontier challenge, requiring consideration of catalytic mechanism and optimization across biochemical and biophysical criteria. Here, we present dEVA (design by EVolutionary Algorithm), a multi-objective protein design method built on principles drawn from evolutionary biology. We apply dEVA to the zero-shot, de novo design of metalloenzymes by optimizing the coordination sphere of catalytic metals. We characterize a bi-zinc metalloenzyme that exhibits promiscuous hydrolytic activity towards both phosphomonoesters and phosphodiesters. This design achieves a rate enhancement ((k cat /K M )/k w ) of up to 3 x 10 13 relative to the uncatalyzed reaction, comparable to characterized natural phosphatases. Structural characterization via x-ray crystallography and absorption spectroscopy supports the design of a de novo active site. These results demonstrate that de novo enzymes can be designed without pre-specified motifs, natural templates, or evolutionary information.

shortlist.title: Combinatorial Approach to Circuit Complexity: From Approximate Quantum Codes to Lieb-Schultz-Mattis Constraints
shortlist.abstract: Approximate quantum error correction (AQEC) provides a versatile framework for both quantum information processing and probing many-body entanglement. We reveal a fundamental tension between the error-correcting power of an AQEC and the hardness of code state preparation. More precisely, through a novel application of the Lovász local lemma, we establish a fundamental tradeoff between local indistinguishability and circuit complexity, showing that orthogonal short-range entangled states must be distinguishable via a local operator. These results offer a powerful tool for exploring quantum circuit complexity across diverse settings. As applications, we derive stronger constraints on the complexity of AQEC codes with transversal logical gates and establish strong complexity lower bounds for W state preparation. Our framework also provides a novel perspective for systems with Lieb-Schultz-Mattis type constraints.

shortlist.title: Topological Quantum Criticality in the Quasiperiodic Cluster Ising Chain
shortlist.abstract: Topological classifications of quantum critical systems have recently attracted growing interest, as they go beyond the traditional paradigms of condensed matter and statistical physics. However, such classifications remain largely unexplored in aperiodic environments, particularly under quasiperiodic modulations. In this Letter, we uncover a family of topological quasiperiodic fixed points with critical scalings intermediate between the clean and infinite-randomness limits. By exactly solving the quasiperiodic cluster Ising chain, we demonstrate that all phase boundaries separating quasiperiodically modulated phases are governed by topological Ising-like fixed points unique to strongly modulated quasiperiodic systems. Although their local bulk critical properties match those of conventional quasiperiodic Ising critical points reported before, these fixed points host robust topological edge degeneracies and exhibit a distinct symmetry-enriched realization of the quasiperiodic Ising criticality, as further supported by complementary lattice simulations.

In this comment we demonstrate that both features are indeed present in the Dicke-Ising model for the investigated parameter range in Ref. [1].

shortlist.title: The Life and Death of Stars that Capture Primordial Black Holes
shortlist.abstract: Primordial black holes (PBHs) in the asteroid mass window (10 17 –10 23 g) remain viable dark matter candidates and can be captured by stars. We develop the first global framework for the evolution of stars that capture PBHs, combining analytic calculations, stellar evolution models, 3D general-relativistic magnetohydrodynamic simulations, and Monte Carlo population synthesis. We find that the fate of these systems bifurcates: PBHs that form an accretion disk before consuming the host drive explosive disruption, whereas PBHs captured too late or growing too slowly consume the star quietly. Capture is dominated by three-body interactions with planetary or stellar companions. For a solar-type host with a Jupiter analog, inspiral within a main-sequence lifetime requires M BH crit ≳ 1 0 22 g , while lighter PBHs generally require tighter companions. Once deposited at the center, the PBH grows through inefficient quasi-spherical Bondi accretion; if it reaches the angular-momentum threshold before consuming the host, the inflow circularizes into a disk. Our Monte Carlo calculations yield sizable quiet-consumption and explosive-disruption populations, with final PBH masses M BH ∼ 0.01–1 M ⊙ and disk-forming PBH spins a * ≈ 0.8. Disk formation is the point of no return: disk winds and relativistic jets of ∼10 45 –10 50 erg s −1 disrupt the star within minutes. The resulting transients may include a ∼day-long UV/blue signal, radio afterglow, and, if the jet escapes, an X-ray-flash (XRF)/low-luminosity gamma-ray-burst (llGRB) signal. For an O ( 1 ) PBH dark matter fraction and optimistic capture assumptions, the event rate can reach that of llGRBs. The low-mass, high-spin remnants offer a complementary PBH probe and possible source for subsolar black hole mergers.

shortlist.title: Structural and regulatory evolution across the genus Hordeum
shortlist.abstract: The genus Hordeum comprises cultivated barley and its wild relatives, an evolutionarily, ecologically and agriculturally important group of grasses 1,2 . Here we generated a chromosome-scale comparative genomic resource comprising all recognized diploid Hordeum species together with representative polyploid lineages. Comparative analyses reveal extensive structural variation, including inversions and chromosomal rearrangements that disrupt proximal collinearity and reflect lineage-specific genome remodelling. Single-copy gene phylogenies identify ancient hybridization, segmental exchange and introgression, revealing pervasive reticulate evolution during Hordeum diversification. We uncover widespread horizontal gene transfer from Panicoideae grasses into Hordeum , with many transferred genes showing evidence of transcription and functional integration. Retrotransposon proliferation explains genome size variation and provides insights into polyploid genome evolution. Whole-genome alignments reveal contrasting evolutionary dynamics: whereas coding sequences remain highly conserved, regulatory elements undergo rapid turnover, providing a rich source of regulatory diversity for phenotypic evolution. Case studies of vernalization and glume development demonstrate how natural variation in regulatory and coding sequences contributes to flowering time and floral morphology. This comprehensive pangenomic framework establishes Hordeum as a model for studying genome evolution, structural variation and the genetic basis of adaptive traits, offering new avenues for barley improvement.

shortlist.title: Evidence for late Middle Pleistocene Homo erectus in mainland East Asia
shortlist.abstract: Hominin fossils and genetic evidence indicate that several hominin populations occupied East and Southeast Asia during the Middle and Late Pleistocene epoch1–10. Homo erectus fossils remain scarce in southern China and mainland Southeast Asia4,8,11. Here we report nine newly discovered late Middle Pleistocene hominin teeth from the Naxian and Baxian caves at the Chongzuo study area, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, southern China, dated to around 324–184 thousand years ago12. Palaeoproteomics reveals the presence of an endogenous dental proteome in all five hominin teeth studied molecularly. Four teeth contain a derived H. erectus substitution in ameloblastin that to date has been observed only in older Middle Pleistocene H. erectus specimens from China13. The proteomes of these four teeth differ from the previous H. erectus proteomes from China at another ameloblastin position, suggesting that these specimens represent a previously unsampled H. erectus population. Morphometric and geometric morphometric methods support an attribution of these teeth to H. erectus, as well as four additional teeth. This fills a gap in the geographical and chronological distribution of H. erectus in East Asia. The fifth tooth studied proteomically, PA1796, is morphologically distinct from H. erectus, Neanderthals (Homo neanderthalensis) and modern humans (Homo sapiens), and does not contain the H. erectus-derived amino acid sequence. The late survival of H. erectus on mainland East Asia suggests that at least two hominin lineages, H. erectus and Homo longi (Denisovans)6,7, possibly represented by PA1796, were present in the region towards the end of the Middle Pleistocene, with the first documented occurrence of H. sapiens not much later5. shortlist.title: Rainforest adaptation in late Homo erectus from southern China
shortlist.abstract: Homo erectus represents one of the longest-persisting hominin species, with a geographic range from Africa to eastern Eurasia from approximately 1.9 million years ago 1 to 108 thousand years ago (ka) 2 . Despite this, there are still large gaps in our understanding of the adaptation capabilities of this species and the extent of its persistence in China. Assumptions over ecological preferences based on the Trinil 3 , Sangiran 4 and Ngandong 2 (in Java) open woodland–grassland mosaics have persisted, combined with limited direct stable carbon isotope measurements in Asia. Here we present a rich temporal and environmental context for nine hominin teeth, eight of which were morphologically and genetically identified as H. erectus 5 , found in two sister caves in Guangxi province, southern China. We modelled 43 radiometric ages from five dating techniques to establish a timeline for H. erectus presence in this region. Stable and clumped isotopes and trace elements from teeth were used to establish the dominant environments and their behavioural responses. We show that H. erectus was present in southern China between 324 and 184 ka, which is substantially more recent than previously established in this region for unequivocally H. erectus fossils at approximately 400 ka. The evidence suggests that they were persisting in closed rainforest ecosystems, thought to be the domain of only Homo sapiens , and were demonstrating long-term mobility and ecological flexibility. This evidence challenges the assumptions over the ecological preferences and behavioural limitations of H. erectus .
