shortlist.title: Multiscale Modeling of Virus Capsid Self-Assembly Reveals How Small Molecule Antivirals Can Redirect Assembly Pathways and Products
shortlist.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
shortlist.abstract: Controlling the assembly of a virus capsid, a regular complex of hundreds of subunits, has applications for development of antivirals and for development of nanocontainers. Recent work has shown that a class of small molecules called capsid assembly modulators (CAMs) is promising for treating Hepatitis B virus (HBV). CAMs bind to HBV capsid proteins and alter their self-assembly, leading to nonfunctional and malformed structures. The mechanisms by which CAMs alter capsid assembly remain unclear. Here, we use a kinetic Monte Carlo (KMC) model for HBV capsid assembly to simulate how CAMs affect this complex reaction. The model is parametrized from all-atom simulations, resulting in unprecedented correlation between simulation and biochemical and structural observations. Simulations reproduce the effect of CAMs on experimental assembly products and their distributions. By analyzing assembly trajectories, we clarify the roles of thermodynamics and kinetics in determining assembly products, identify assembly mechanisms, and predict the key intermediates that lead to either capsids or malformed structures. Our findings enhance our fundamental understanding of capsid assembly, help advance the development of CAMs as a treatment for HBV and, more broadly, inform efforts to direct self-assembly pathways toward specific products.

shortlist.title: Time-dependent Cosmic-Ray Escape from Wind Bubbles: Hard Spectra Formation
shortlist.abstract: Wind-driven bubbles are dynamic systems that can accelerate cosmic rays, depending on their physical properties, up to very high energies (VHE). We investigate how a time-dependent description of the particle transport may impact the escaping cosmic-ray flux. The wind bubble system is modeled as spherically symmetric. Cosmic rays are continuously injected at the position of the termination shock and propagate through advection and diffusion until the escape at the time-dependent position of the forward shock, which is treated as a free escape boundary. The one-dimensional spherical time-dependent transport equation is solved by transforming it into the corresponding set of stochastic differential equations (SDEs) and integrated with a modified version of the open source cosmic-ray propagation framework CRPropa. We find that, during the wind driven phase, the downstream escaping spectra from wind bubbles can be harder than ∼ E −2 , the conventional expectation from diffusive shock acceleration (DSA). Depending on the turbulence model, the initial energy spectrum can be significantly suppressed at the lowest energies, which could be an observable feature to distinguish between different turbulence realizations. This effect could lead to an efficient confinement of low energy particles, potentially leading to observable implication in terms of multimessenger radiation and cosmic-ray accumulated grammage within the bubble.

shortlist.title: Resolving Ultrafast Electronic and Chiral Structural Dynamics That Govern Circularly Polarized Luminescence from Eu(III) Antenna Complexes
shortlist.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
shortlist.abstract: Circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) from chiral molecules and materials has promising applications in display technology, optical sensing, and quantum information science. However, luminescent-state configurations that approach the maximum degree of circular polarization in emission have only been achieved in exceptional cases, most notably in Eu(III) antenna complexes. An open challenge is the understanding and suppression of detrimental relaxation dynamics of the CPL-active state, which can distort carefully designed ground-state configurations and quench luminescence. We now resolve these processes for the prototypical Eu(III) antenna complex CsEu((+,−)-hfbc)4 (hfbc = 3-heptafluorobutyrylcamphorate) by mapping its complete electronic and chiral structural evolution with ultrafast circular dichroism spectroscopy. Combined with transient absorption measurements and electronic structure calculations, we unravel the intramolecular energy transfer from the helically arranged antenna ligands to the emissive metal ion, and extract the stereochemical configuration of all involved excited states through their ligand-centered circular dichroism. We find that population transfer proceeds from delocalized singlet excitonic states via a ligand-localized triplet, while a parallel singlet exciton trapping channel unexpectedly quenches luminescence. Remarkably, excitation of the luminescent Eu(III) ion increases the helical twist of the ligand sphere by 2.7 ± 1.3° toward an ideal square-antiprismatic geometry, where the CPL performance is most favorable. The excited 4f-orbitals thus drive non-negligible changes in the primary coordination sphere, challenging common assumptions in 4f coordination chemistry and elucidating the need for ligand antenna rigidification to maximize…

shortlist.title: PEARLS: NuSTAR and XMM-Newton Extragalactic Survey of the JWST North Ecliptic Pole Time-domain Field V: Unraveling X-Ray Spectral Variability
shortlist.abstract: As one of the first deep time-domain surveys in the hard X-ray band, the NuSTAR campaign in the JWST North Ecliptic Pole Time Domain Field (NEP-TDF) offers a prime opportunity to measure variability in a faint population of active galactic nuclei (AGN) in the medium- to high-redshift Universe. In the X-ray band, AGN variability is generally caused by changes in the brightness of the corona ( F int variability) or changes in the column density of obscuring material near the supermassive black hole (SMBH; N H variability). Broadband spectroscopy (∼0.5–24 keV) is required to reliably disentangle these two phenomena. With simultaneous NuSTAR and XMM-Newton coverage—as well as 1.8 Ms of Chandra monitoring—the X-ray surveys in the NEP-TDF are ideally situated for this purpose. This work presents the first spectral modeling of the 52 NuSTAR-identified sources discovered in the latter half of the campaign, as well as a spectroscopic variability study of the entire 112-source NuSTAR NEP-TDF catalog. Seven variable candidates are identified. We find that ≳1000 total counts split across many (≳10) epochs are needed in order to detect variability. Additionally, variable sources are compared to the survey sensitivity in order to inform population synthesis models of how variations can affect the detectability of faint AGN, which dominate the SMBH accretion history. Lastly, the timescale of N H variability is investigated as a probe for the obscurer location. Significant variability is slightly more common on >100 day timescales, suggesting that the torus may have only slight dominance in driving N H variability in faint AGN.

shortlist.title: Tracing Radial Structures of Molecular Gas and Gas-phase Metallicity across the Galaxy Merger Sequence with KILOGAS
shortlist.abstract: Galaxy interactions and mergers are expected to redistribute baryons across galactic disks, yet how molecular gas and metals are reorganized as a function of merger stage remains unclear. In this work, we investigate the radial structure of molecular gas and gas-phase metallicity (oxygen abundance traced by O3N2 ) using a large sample of nearby galaxies from the Kiloparsec Investigations of Local Objects’ Gas And Star formation (KILOGAS) survey spanning a wide range of interaction stages. We construct galaxy-by-galaxy radial profiles of molecular gas surface density and metallicity and characterize their shapes. We find that a significant fraction of gas-rich, star-forming galaxies, regardless of merger stage, deviates from simple single-slope profiles, and that molecular gas and metallicity do not always evolve in a coupled manner. The inner molecular gas profiles become progressively steeper along the merger sequence relative to matched control galaxies, with the strongest deviations observed in postmerger systems. The outer profiles, meanwhile, become flatter, consistent with merger-driven inflows redistributing gas toward the center. Metallicity profiles also tend to steepen with advancing merger stage, particularly in the inner regions, while exhibiting no systematic change in the outer regions relative to control galaxies. This weaker and more spatially limited metallicity response likely reflects the combined effects of gas inflow, chemical enrichment, and mixing, which operate on different timescales and can partially offset one another. Overall, our results establish radial profile shapes as a powerful diagnostic of baryon redistribution in galaxy interactions.

shortlist.title: Directed Attachment of Catalysts into the Extended Environments of Soft Photoelectrodes for Hydrogen Evolution
shortlist.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
shortlist.abstract: We present a detailed investigation of early stage photoelectrochemical deposition of platinum nanoparticle (Pt-NP) catalysts on semiconducting polymer platforms for the light-assisted hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) using electrochemical, spectroscopic, and microscopy characterization, combined with density functional theory (DFT) modeling. The photoactive junction─formed from a blend of donor (PTB7-Th) and acceptor (P(NDI2OD-T2)) polymers─exhibits HER efficiencies that increase exponentially with Pt-NP loading (ca. 8.0 × 101 to 2.5 × 104 ng/cm2) of highly faceted Pt-NPs. The blended heterojunction demonstrates acceptor enrichment of the near-surface region as the point of Pt deposition via progressive nucleation, at sites which we posit are the near-surface termini of “fast transport pathways” created within the PTB7-Th/P(NDI2OD-T2) blend film. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), for the lowest coverage Pt-NPs, combined with DFT modeling, suggests Pt–S interactions via the bithiophene groups in P(NDI2OD-T2) might dominate at the earliest stages of Pt deposition, while larger DFT-modeled 14- and 38-atom Pt clusters demonstrate Pt–C and Pt–O═C interactions on naphthalene diimide cores. Collectively, our findings suggest that submicron environments in soft photoelectrode materials function as integrated architectures, as expected, where charge creation requires well mixed domains, adjacent to domains optimized for charge transport. Photoelectrochemically deposited metals such as Pt-NPs decorate the most photoelectrochemically active near-surface regions, producing good HER efficiencies. Hierarchical assembly of such photoactive soft materials has the potential to provide a transformative framework for scalable energy conversion that extends beyond hydrogen…

shortlist.title: Divergent activation of the RXFP1 relaxin receptor by protein and small-molecule agonists
shortlist.abstract: The relaxin receptor RXFP1 is a therapeutic target owing to its potential benefits in the treatment of fibrosis and heart failure. Protein and small-molecule agonists are currently in midstage clinical trials for various forms of heart disease. In this work, we present three cryo–electron microscopy structures of RXFP1: ligand-free, bound to the native agonist relaxin-2, and bound to the small-molecule drug candidate AZD5462. These structures reveal that relaxin-2 engages the receptor’s ectodomain, whereas AZD5462 binds to the transmembrane domain. Together with hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry, we show that relaxin-2 induces reorganization of the linker domain into a helical secondary structure. By contrast, AZD5462 stabilizes an active conformation through a distinct set of conformational rearrangements. Altogether, our findings define divergent activation mechanisms for protein and small-molecule agonists of RXFP1.

shortlist.title: Unemployment Benefits and Unemployment in the Great Recession: The Role of Equilibrium Effects
shortlist.abstract: Equilibrium labor market theory suggests that unemployment benefit extensions affect unemployment by impacting both job search decisions by the unemployed and job creation decisions by employers. The existing empirical literature focused on the former effect only. We develop a new methodology necessary to incorporate the measurement of the latter effect. Implementing this methodology in the data, we find that benefit extensions raise equilibrium wages and lead to a sharp contraction in vacancy creation and employment and a rise in unemployment.
shortlist.topic: Labor market dynamics and wage inequality

shortlist.title: Conservation of the tumour microenvironment across organs and species
shortlist.abstract: Current understanding of the host tissue response to solid tumours is largely based on investigations of tumour types in isolation 1 . Given the breadth and diversity of human tumour pathology and contributions of tumour microenvironment (TME) cells to disease progression, pan-cancer analysis is needed to bridge major themes of stromal and immune cell evolution. To date, however, efforts to compare the TME response across cancers have been limited in scope 2 , 3 . Here we conduct a comprehensive pan-cancer analysis by algorithmically screening thousands of publicly available single-cell transcriptomic datasets for stromal and immune signatures across species and tissue types. We demonstrate conserved hallmarks of host cell transcriptional programming in response to malignancy across 42 cancer types in more than 2,000 human and mouse tumour samples. These findings are codified as an interactive web atlas ( tmeatlas.stanford.edu ) and software package (scTME) that will serve as practical resources for the systematic interrogation of the TME in tumours.

shortlist.title: 8-Oxoguanine Is the Major Product of the Reaction of Guanine Radical Cations with •NO2: A Spin-Orchestrated, Anisotropic Reaction Landscape and Its Biological Implications
shortlist.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
shortlist.abstract: Formation of guanine radical cations (G•+) represents a hallmark DNA lesion produced by ionizing radiation and one-electron oxidation processes. •NO2, a reactive nitrogen species in living systems, drives nitrative and oxidative damage linked to mutagenesis and inflammation. Herein, we delineate spin-orchestrated interactions between •NO2 and radical cations of 2′-deoxyguanosine (dGuo•+) and its model compound 9-methylguanine (9MG•+) to probe synergistic pathways that exacerbate guanine nucleobase and nucleoside damage. Kinetic energy-resolved reaction coupled with mass spectrometric measurements revealed distinct pathways governing regioselective nitrite- and nitro-additions, adduct decomposition, and charge transfer. Direct dynamics simulations and potential energy surface analyses of the 9MG•+ + •NO2 model system, using spin-projected and time-dependent DFT, CCSD(T), and CASPT2 theories, characterized reaction mechanisms, thermodynamics, and kinetics arising from anisotropic interactions within open-shell 1,OS[G•+(↑)···(↓)•NO2] and 3[G•+(↑)···(↑)•NO2]. Through radical combination, the reaction system advances through multiple excited electronic and vibrational manifolds while preserving spin states (no intersystem crossing); only singlet states are open to chemical transformations. •NO2 markedly amplifies the lesion of guanine radicals by promoting sequential electron and H loss, producing 8-oxoguanine in neutral, radical cation, and doubly oxidized forms, along with release of •NO, NO+, and HNO. These pathways proceed through nitrite addition rather than guanine nitration, and HNO forms through •NO-mediated hydrogen abstraction via both conventional and roaming mechanisms. The studies identified new routes to the 8-oxoguanine lesion that has been traditionally…

shortlist.title: Development and Application of Nanopore Direct RNA Sequencing
shortlist.abstract: Individual RNA strands can be sequenced directly using nanoscale protein pores. This process, Nanopore Direct RNA Sequencing (Nanopore DRS), uses a helicase motor protein to regulate RNA displacement through the nanopore orifice in single nucleotide steps. Partial blockade of the monovalent ionic current is recorded at 4 kHz and converted to a string of RNA nucleotide basecalls using machine learning models. In this review, we discuss the development of Nanopore DRS from 1996 to the present. This includes performance metrics, evolution of machine learning models, and applications of Nanopore DRS to major RNA classes across kingdoms. Advantages of the technology are highlighted with special emphasis on nucleotide modifications along intact single strands. Shortcomings of the technology are also considered along with possible solutions. We close with forward looking Nanopore DRS applications: Single cell RNA sequencing; remote monitoring of infectious agents; principled understanding of nanopore ionic current patterns using all-atoms simulations; global food security; and clinical applications.

shortlist.title: Assessing Multiple Treatment Regimens for Tuberculosis
shortlist.abstract: MethodsIn this phase 2, randomized, controlled trial, we assigned participants with rifampin-susceptible pulmonary tuberculosis to receive the standard four-drug combination (isoniazid–rifampin–pyrazinamide–ethambutol; HRZE) for 24 weeks; bedaquiline–delamanid–moxifloxacin for 16 weeks; or one of 10 new four-drug combinations for 16 weeks. The new regimens contained ganfeborole, BTZ-043, or both, with combinations of bedaquiline, delamanid, moxifloxacin, pyrazinamide, pretomanid, and linezolid. The primary end point was the log10(time to positivity) slope (rate of change from baseline to week 12 in the time to Mycobacterium tuberculosis growth in a positive sputum culture). The treatment effect was assessed as the Bayesian posterior probability of superiority of each new regimen to HRZE with respect to the primary end point (results were used to select regimens for further evaluation, rather than for characterization of efficacy). ResultsA total of 401 participants underwent randomization; 371 were included in the modified intention-to-treat population and 400 in the safety population. We identified two promising regimens for further evaluation: ganfeborole–bedaquiline–pretomanid–moxifloxacin (BPMG) and BTZ-043–bedaquiline–delamanid–moxifloxacin (BDMT). The log10(time to positivity) slope was 0.129 log10(days) per week (95% Bayesian credible interval, 0.112 to 0.146) with BPMG and 0.142 log10(days) per week (95% Bayesian credible interval, 0.126 to 0.160) with BDMT, as compared with 0.118 log10(days) per week (95% Bayesian credible interval, 0.105 to 0.131) with HRZE, for a relative difference of 9.1% (95% Bayesian credible interval, −8.6 to 29.0) and 20.5% (95% Bayesian credible interval, 2.7 to 41.1), respectively, and a posterior probability of superiority of 0.83…

shortlist.title: Balancing redox-mediated cytotoxicity and catalysis in natural product biosynthesis
shortlist.abstract: Redox-mediated chemistry is central to both the biosynthesis and cytotoxicity of many natural products, yet how microbes balance these processes remains poorly understood. Here, we uncover a conserved mechanism that coordinates three redox-mediated processes in secondary metabolite biosynthesis: self-protection, prevention of substrate degradation, and late-stage biosynthesis. Using the antitumor antibiotic doxorubicin as a model system, we show that the vicinal oxygen chelate (VOC) protein DnrV prevents reactive oxygen species formation and substrate degradation while promoting P450 catalysis. We expand this paradigm to a conserved family of VOC-fold proteins, redox-associated cytotoxin-binding proteins (REACT), found across bacteria, fungi, and plants. REACT represents a multifunctional protein class that balances antibiotic assembly, self-protection, and prevention of metabolite destruction, providing a foundational understanding of production of redox-active natural products.

shortlist.title: Equity in Maternal–Fetal Medicine — Technological Advances and a Potential Path Forward
shortlist.abstract: Without safeguards, rapid technological development in maternal–fetal medicine could reinforce existing racial, socioeconomic, and geographic inequities in prenatal care.

shortlist.title: Substitution Reactions of Halogen-Substituted Acetals: Glycosylations and Related Reactions
shortlist.abstract: The nucleophilic substitution reactions of halogen-substituted acetals are useful for the synthesis of a variety of compounds, most particularly of sugar derivatives. This review will summarize the current understanding of the mechanisms involved in these reactions and will present substitution reactions of carbohydrate derivatives with fluorine, chlorine, bromine, and iodine substituents. The halogen atom at C-2 can have a powerful influence on the stereoselectivities of the glycosylation reactions, most often leading to 1,2-trans stereoselectivity. Examples of the uses of these halogen-substituted products will also be provided.

shortlist.title: Diffusion Models for Small-Molecule Design
shortlist.abstract: Diffusion models (DMs) have emerged as a class of generative models for controllable small-molecule design in drug discovery capable of progressively transforming noisy or partially specified molecular states into candidate structures under structural, geometric, and property constraints. This Review provides a comprehensive overview of the methodological foundations and representative applications of diffusion-based molecular generation, emphasizing the alignment among molecular representations, generative dynamics, controllable design, and evaluation and validation. Particular attention is given to recent advances in property- and structure-guided generation, target-aware and fragment-based design, multiobjective optimization, and synthesis-aware generation. We also discuss the roles of data sets, computational evaluation, and prospective experiments in assessing the chemical and biological relevance of generated molecules. By organizing these developments within a unified conceptual framework, we provide computational chemists and drug discovery researchers with a structured roadmap that balances the mathematical rigor with chemical intuition. Throughout, we highlight current methodological limitations and unresolved challenges and conclude with future directions toward chemically credible and experimentally grounded molecular design. To facilitate navigation of this rapidly evolving field, we introduce an interactive companion platform (https://diffsmd.scbdd.com) that provides a curated, continuously updated repository of model architectures and visualizations.

shortlist.title: Transition metal-catalyzed carborane cage B–H activation and functionalization: a mechanistic view
shortlist.abstract: B-H activation affects the energy level of further functionalization, and thus the selectivity is determined by B-H activation or subsequent functionalization. Therefore, the factors dictating selectivity can be identified by analyzing the transition state properties, providing insights into improving regio- or chiral-at-cage selectivities. The opportunities and challenges for future research are discussed. We highlight strategies of exploiting the unique characteristics of carboranes based on C-H bond activation protocols and single-electron transfer approaches including photo- and electrocatalysis. We expect that this review will provide a framework for understanding the catalytic mechanism, rational catalyst design, and exploration of precise functionalization strategies.

shortlist.title: Fault-Tolerant Execution of Error-Corrected Quantum Algorithms
shortlist.abstract: Scaling up quantum algorithms to tackle high-impact problems in science and industry requires quantum error correction and fault tolerance. While progress has been made in experimentally realizing error-corrected primitives, the end-to-end execution of logical quantum algorithms using only fault-tolerant (FT) components has remained out of reach. We demonstrate the FT and error-corrected execution of two quantum algorithms, the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) and the Harrow-Hassidim-Lloyd algorithm applied to the Poisson equation, on Quantinuum H2 and Helios trapped-ion quantum processors using the ⟦ 7 , 1 , 3 ⟧ Steane code. For QAOA circuits on five and six logical qubits, we show performance improvements from increasing the number of QAOA layers and the number of T gates used to approximate logical rotations, despite increased physical circuit complexity. We further show that QAOA circuits with up to eight logical qubits and nine logical T gates perform similarly to unencoded circuits. For the largest QAOA circuits we run, with 12 logical (97 physical) qubits and 2132 physical two-qubit gates, we still observe better-than-random performance. Finally, we show that adding active quantum error correction cycles and increasing the repeat-until-success limit of state-preparation subroutines can improve the performance of a quantum algorithm, thereby demonstrating critical capabilities of scalable FT quantum computation. Our results are enabled by a FT logical T -gate implementation with an infidelity of 2.7 ( 4 ) × 10 − 3 and dynamic circuits with measurement-dependent feedback. Our work demonstrates near-breakeven performance of complex, error-corrected algorithmic quantum circuits using only FT components.

shortlist.title: Revertant Autograft Replacement in Recessive Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa
shortlist.abstract: Two adolescents with epidermolysis bullosa received autografts from revertant skin, which provided durable epidermal replacement over approximately 95% of the body-surface area in one patient and 50% in the other.

shortlist.title: Redox metabolism at the host–pathogen interface in Mycobacterium tuberculosis
shortlist.abstract: Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) persists within the host despite robust immune responses and prolonged multidrug therapy, underscoring the need to better understand the mechanisms that drive persistence and treatment failure. Emerging evidence indicates that redox metabolism is a central interface governing host-pathogen interactions during tuberculosis (TB). This review discusses how redox cross talk integrates immune signaling with bacterial physiology through interconnected pathways involving iron metabolism, lipid peroxidation, mitochondrial bioenergetics, central carbon metabolism, and antioxidant defenses. We highlight how these processes generate physiological, metabolic, and spatial heterogeneity within infected macrophages and granulomas, promoting bacterial persistence, drug tolerance, and tissue pathology. Finally, we discuss therapeutic strategies targeting redox-dependent vulnerabilities in both the host and the pathogen, including modulation of macrophage bioenergetics, nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2) signaling, ferroptosis, and mycobacterial respiration. Integrating host and bacterial redox biology provides a unified framework for developing host-directed and pathogen-directed interventions to improve TB treatment and limit long-term disease sequelae.

shortlist.title: Rising Wages and the Decline of Low-Wage Work
shortlist.abstract: From 2014 to 2024, the share of U.S. hourly workers paid below $15 in real terms fell by two-thirds, from 38 percent to 13 percent. Why? We first distinguish the entry and exit of employers—wherein high-paying employers have supplanted low-paying ones—from organizational changes among incumbent employers. Organizational changes can be imposed on employers by external constraints, like labor market tightness, or emerge from the pursuit of new opportunities. Using panel data drawn from administrative records and job reviews, we bring this framework to bear on the recent wage gains at the bottom of the labor market. Contrary to predictions of creative destruction, we can trace only a small amount of these wage gains to the disappearance of low-wage organizations. Instead, the main driver of rising pay was low- and middle-paying incumbent employers of low-wage occupations increasing pay. These gains in low-wage occupations were associated with tightening labor markets and increased minimum wages. But over and above these external constraints, employers also pursued new opportunities for reorganizing work in low-skill jobs. Notwithstanding organizational inertia, major gains for workers’ pay can come from changes in existing workplaces.
shortlist.topic: Labor market dynamics and wage inequality

shortlist.title: Noninvertible Bosonic Chiral Symmetry on the Lattice
shortlist.abstract: In this work, we realize the 3 + 1 D noninvertible Z N chiral symmetry generator as an operator in a many-body lattice Hilbert space. A crucial ingredient in our construction is the use of infinite-dimensional U(1) rotor site Hilbert spaces. Specifically, our Hilbert space is that of a U(1) lattice gauge theory coupled to a charge 1 scalar in the Villain formulation, which allows for direct access to monopoles and for a simple definition of a magnetic Z N one-form symmetry Z m ( 1 ) , at the lattice Hamiltonian level. We construct the generator of the Z N chiral symmetry as a locality-preserving unitary operator not in the entire Hilbert space but only in the subspace of Z m ( 1 ) -invariant states. Using a lattice-level duality based on gauging Z m ( 1 ) , we find a dual description of this subspace, as the subspace of a charge 1 / N gauge theory invariant under an electric one-form symmetry Z e ( 1 ) . We show that, in this dual formulation, the chiral symmetry generator extends unitarily to the entire Hilbert space but has a mixed anomaly with the Z e ( 1 ) symmetry.

shortlist.title: Realization of a Cavity-Coupled Rydberg Array
shortlist.abstract: Scalable quantum computers and quantum networks require the combination of quantum processing nodes with efficient light-matter interfaces to distribute quantum information in local or long-distance quantum networks. Neutral-atom arrays have both been coupled to Rydberg states to enable high-fidelity quantum gates in universal processing architectures, and to optical cavities to realize interfaces to photons. However, combining these two capabilities and coupling atom arrays to highly excited Rydberg states in the mode of an optical cavity has been an outstanding challenge. Here we present a novel cavity-coupled Rydberg array that achieves this long-standing goal. We prepare, detect, and control individual atoms in a scalable optical tweezer array, couple them strongly to the optical mode of a high-finesse optical cavity and excite them in a controlled way to Rydberg states. We show that high-cooperativity coupling to an optical cavity—demonstrated via the dispersive shift of the resonance of the cavity in presence of the atoms—and strong Rydberg interactions—demonstrated via the collective enhancement of Rydberg coupling in the atomic array—can be achieved in our setup at the same spatial location. Our presented experimental platform opens the path to several new directions, including the realization of quantum network nodes, quantum simulation of long-range interacting, open quantum systems, and photonic-state engineering leveraging high-fidelity Rydberg control.

shortlist.title: Market Response to Racial Uprisings
shortlist.abstract: Do investors anticipate that demands for racial equity will impact companies? We explore this question in the context of the Black Lives Matter (BLM) movement—the largest racially motivated protest movement in U.S. history—and its effect on the U.S. policing industry using a novel dataset on publicly traded firms contracting with the police. It is unclear whether the BLM uprisings were likely to increase or decrease market valuations of firms contracting heavily with police because of the increased interest in reforming the police, fears over rising crime, and pushes to “defund the police”. We find, in contrast to the predictions of economics experts we surveyed, that in the three weeks following incidents triggering BLM uprisings, policing firms experienced a stock price increase of seven percentage points relative to the stock prices of nonpolicing firms in similar industries. In particular, firms producing surveillance technology and police accountability tools experienced higher returns following BLM activism–related events. Furthermore, policing firms’ fundamentals, such as sales, improved after the murder of George Floyd, suggesting that policing firms’ future performances bore out investors' positive expectations following incidents triggering BLM uprisings. Our research shows how—despite BLM’s calls to reduce investment in policing and explore alternative public safety approaches—the financial market has translated high-profile violence against Black civilians and calls for systemic change into shareholder gains and additional revenues for police suppliers.

shortlist.title: Realization of Repulsive Polarons in the Strongly Correlated Regime
shortlist.abstract: Mobile impurities interacting with a quantum medium form quasiparticles known as polarons, a central concept in many-body physics. While the quantum impurity problem has been extensively studied with ultracold atomic gases, repulsive polarons in the strongly correlated regime have remained elusive. Typically, the impurity atoms bind into molecules or rapidly decay into deeper-lying states before they can acquire an appreciable dressing cloud. Here, we report on the realization of polarons in a strongly repulsive two-dimensional quantum gas. Using a superfluid of Li 6 dimers, we introduce impurities by promoting a small fraction of the dimers into higher levels of the transverse confining potential. These novel synthetic-spin polarons give access to the strongly repulsive regime where common decay channels are suppressed. We extract key polaron properties—the energy, quasiparticle residue, and effective mass—using trap modulation and Bragg spectroscopy. Our measurements are well captured by a microscopic T -matrix approach and quantum Monte Carlo simulations, revealing deviations from mean-field predictions. In particular, we measure a significant enhancement of the polaron mass, with values exceeding twice the free-dimer mass. Our demonstration of a stable repulsive Bose polaron establishes a platform for studying impurity physics in low-dimensional and strongly correlated systems.

shortlist.abstract: We present an optical–infrared variability study of two isolated narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies, Mrk 42 and Mrk 493, using ZTF optical and WISE/NEOWISE W1/W2 light curves, supplemented by ATLAS, SDSS, Swift, and IAC80 data. We analyse colour–magnitude and flux–flux relations and measure optical–infrared reverberation lags using flux-randomisation and random-subset-selection (FR/RSS) realisations of the interpolated cross-correlation function after correcting the WISE light curves for the variable accretion-disc contribution. For Mrk 42, we obtain observed-frame lags of 54⁺¹³₋₃₃ and 62⁺⁷₋₃₅ d in W1 and W2, respectively. After applying the redshift/wavelength correction, these correspond to dust-response radii of 0.045^(+0.011)_(-0.028) and 0.052^(+0.006)_(-0.029) pc. For Mrk 493, the corresponding observed-frame lags are 94⁺¹⁸₋₂₁ and 111⁺²⁶₋₂₄ d, giving corrected dust-response radii of 0.078^(+0.015)_(-0.017) and 0.092^(+0.021)_(-0.020) pc, respectively. Both galaxies show optical bluer-when-brighter behaviour, whereas their W1 − W2 responses differ: the relation is significant in Mrk 493 but not in Mrk 42, where host and circumnuclear dilution may be stronger. For Mrk 42, SDSS spectral decomposition provides a host-corrected active galactic nucleus (AGN) luminosity for the contextual broad-line region (BLR) comparison. The measured dust-response radii are broadly consistent with the low-luminosity extension and intrinsic scatter of published Rdust–Lbol relations. The major optical flare in Mrk 42 exhibits four broad internal maxima with an intra-flare timescale of approximately 45–47 d; non-uniform peak intervals and stochastic-model comparisons favour flare substructure within a broader accretion-driven event. Both galaxies follow the expected disc–hot-dust…

shortlist.title: Optimizing phenotype scale improves genetic analyses in large-scale biobanks
shortlist.abstract: Large-scale biobanks have enabled increasingly complicated genetic analyses across thousands of phenotypes. However, studies rarely consider the appropriateness of the phenotype scale, which can drastically affect inference on genetic architecture. Here we introduce SIQReg, which learns a data-driven phenotype scale by minimizing heterogeneity across phenotype quantiles. Across 25 UK Biobank complex traits, SIQReg rejects the default scale for 24. Generally, SIQReg scales lie between default and logarithmic, indicating that traits are neither purely additive nor purely multiplicative. SIQReg improves both nonadditive and additive genetic analyses. It eliminates most nonadditive signals, including 97% of variance quantitative trait loci, indicating that they may be scale-induced, while preserving biologically plausible nonadditive signals. It simultaneously improves power for additive signals, increasing identification of genome-wide association loci and transcriptome-wide association genes by 11% and 13%, respectively, improving polygenic prediction accuracy by 10%, and identifying 50% more high-risk individuals. These gains are replicated across ancestry groups. Our results establish SIQReg as a principled phenotype scale transformation approach that improves genetic analyses of complex traits.

shortlist.title: Dust Formation in Common Envelope Binary Interactions — III. Lightcurves
shortlist.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
shortlist.abstract: Luminous red novae are transient events thought to arise from common envelope binary interactions. In this paper, we perform post-processing light-curve calculations for two, 3D hydrodynamic simulations of common envelope events between 1.7 M⊙ and 3.7 M⊙ asymptotic giant branch stars and a 0.6 M⊙ compact companion, simulated for 44 years under adiabatic conditions, with dust nucleation included. In both our simulations, we observe a bright, hot peak lasting 3–5 years, primarily due to photospheric expansion before and during inspiral. Additional peaks appear for different viewing angles due to the interaction’s asymmetry. Dust forms about 1–3 years after the beginning of the simulated interaction, and shortly afterwards, followed by a partial recovery and a plateau with a colour temperature of ~400 K. The dust photosphere reaches a size of ~250 au by the end of the simulations, but would become optically thin at visible wavelengths in 2000–6000 years, revealing an inner, warmer photosphere. Our results are most reliable around the time of peak and the immediate light decline; outside this window, they remain largely qualitative due to two well-quantified but substantial uncertainties—insufficient surface resolution in the first 1–2 years and the adiabatic assumption in the later years. We finally contextualise our simulations within a group of observed luminous red nova transients, drawing particular attention to the outburst of OGLE-2002-BLG-360 and AT 2025abao, which are the only two luminous red novae to date understood to be the interaction of a companion with low-to-intermediate-mass giant stars.

shortlist.title: Intermediate Input Prices and the Labor Share
shortlist.abstract: We argue that the relative price of materials is an important determinant of the labor share of income. When materials and primary inputs are complements and the profit share is positive, a higher price of materials lowers the labor share and raises the profit share of value added, without requiring markups or returns to scale to change. We show that materials-price fluctuations align with U.S. labor-share trends, provide causal evidence on this mechanism across industries and commuting zones, and quantify its importance in a dynamic quantitative model. Finally, we use our mechanism to rationalize differential labor-share trends across countries. shortlist.title: Collusion through Common Leadership
shortlist.abstract: This paper studies whether common leadership, defined as two firms sharing executives or board directors, contributes to collusion. Using an explicit measure of labor market collusion from unsealed court evidence, we find that the probability of collusion between two firms increases by 11 percentage points after the onset of common leadership, a ninefold increase over the baseline rate. These results are not driven by closeness of product or labor market competition. Our findings are consistent with the increasing attention toward common leadership under Clayton Act Section 8. Institutional subscribers to the NBER working paper series, and residents of developing countries may download this paper without additional charge at www.nber.org.

shortlist.title: A Log-Uniform Initial Magnetic Field Distribution Explains Pulsar and Magnetar Populations through Magnetic Inclination Alignment
shortlist.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
shortlist.abstract: The origin of the gap in the observed magnetic field distribution between pulsars and magnetars raises a challenge to understanding these populations within a unified framework. We analytically show that the gap can be naturally explained by the alignment of the magnetic inclination angle between the magnetic and spin axes. Based on coupled evolution of spin-down and magnetic inclination angle in the plasma-filled magnetosphere, the alignment timescale follows τα∝B−2. Thus, strongly magnetized neutron stars including high-B pulsars and magnetars align more rapidly than pulsars with 1012 G, reducing their beaming fraction and thereby suppressing their observed numbers. However, magnetars are primarily identified through X-ray activity and are therefore relatively less affected by beaming. Taking into account both beaming fraction and luminosity corrections, we reconstruct the initial magnetic field distribution from the observed distribution. We show that pulsars and magnetars do not dictate intrinsically distinct initial distributions, but can instead be understood within a single continuous initial magnetic field distribution, such as a log-uniform distribution.

shortlist.title: Set them free: extending RAMCOAL to model massive black hole triplets in hydrodynamical simulations of galaxies
shortlist.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
shortlist.abstract: Massive black hole binaries (MBHBs) and the higher-order multiples produced by repeated galaxy mergers evolve through regimes that cosmological simulations cannot resolve. These regimes determine merger delays, spins, recoils, and host galaxies at coalescence. We extend the RAMCOAL subgrid model to follow massive black hole triplets within hydrodynamical galaxy simulations. In the original three-stage binary model, black holes evolve as sink particles, undergo dynamical friction, and form bound binaries that harden through stellar scattering, gas torques, circumbinary-disc coupling, and gravitational-wave emission. When a hierarchical triplet becomes chaotic, RAMCOAL samples a library of outcomes from direct N-body experiments and follows the resulting mergers, exchanges, and ejections alongside the accretion and spin evolution of each black hole. Isolated-galaxy tests with different triplet geometries show that orbital configuration alone can change which pair merges and its coalescence time. For the first time, we follow an MBH triplet to coalescence within a hydrodynamical simulation of gas-rich galaxies, coupling triplet-driven mergers to host-galaxy evolution. Subgrid integration costs ≲ 1 ms of single-core time per MBH system and time step, independently of particle resolution. The resulting coalescence properties reflect the environment encountered during subgrid evolution. RAMCOAL thus provides a step towards merger catalogues linking gravitational-wave signatures to the galaxies in which the black holes evolve.

shortlist.title: Enhancing Gradient Inversion Attacks in Federated Learning via Hierarchical Feature Optimization
shortlist.journal: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
shortlist.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) has emerged as a compelling paradigm for privacy-preserving distributed machine learning, allowing multiple clients to collaboratively train a global model by transmitting locally computed gradients to a central server without exposing their private data. Nonetheless, recent studies find that the gradients exchanged in the FL system are also vulnerable to privacy leakage, e.g., an attacker can invert shared gradients to reconstruct sensitive data by leveraging pre-trained generative adversarial networks (GAN) as prior knowledge. However, existing attacks simply perform gradient inversion in the latent space of the GAN model, which limits their expression ability and generalizability. To tackle these challenges, we propose Gradient Inversion over Feature Domains (GIFD), which disassembles the GAN model and searches the hierarchical features of the intermediate layers. Instead of optimizing only over the initial latent code, we progressively change the optimized layer, from the initial latent space to intermediate layers closer to the output images. In addition, we design a regularizer to avoid unreal image generation by adding a small l₁ ball constraint to the searching range. We also extend GIFD to the out-of-distribution (OOD) setting, which weakens the assumption that the training sets of GANs and FL tasks obey the same data distribution. Furthermore, we consider the challenging OOD scenario of label inconsistency and propose a label mapping technique as an effective solution. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method can achieve high-quality reconstruction and outperform competitive baselines across a variety of FL scenarios.

shortlist.title: Burst Spiking Neural Networks
shortlist.journal: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
shortlist.abstract: A central goal of current Spiking Neural Network (SNN) research is to improve their accuracy toward becoming low-power alternatives to Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs). This work further argues that realizing this ambition requires improving not only accuracy but also robustness, defined as the ability to maintain correct predictions under input perturbations. We identify two key issues in existing SNN methods that undermine robustness. First, binary spiking activations can produce large activation-state changes under small perturbations. Second, the lack of effective weight constraints makes network outputs more sensitive to input variations. To this end, we propose Burst Spiking Neural Networks (BuSNNs), built upon Burst-enhanced Spiking Neurons (BSNs) and a Dynamic Weight Constraint (DWC) mechanism. BSNs incorporate burst firing to provide a graded spiking pattern. This spiking mechanism mitigates perturbation-induced transitions in activation states and thereby enhances robustness. DWC penalizes connection weights based on activation states, effectively reducing weight magnitudes and improving robustness while preserving accuracy. We provide theoretical analyses to support these robustness effects. Experimental results further show that, on smaller-scale benchmarks such as CIFAR-10, BuSNNs outperform both SNN and ANN counterparts in accuracy and robustness. On large-scale ImageNet, BuSNN with the MS ResNet-34 backbone further improves top-1 accuracy and corruption robustness over the corresponding SNN baseline by 3.18% and 2.66%, respectively. Despite using spike-based activations, BuSNNs surpass 4-bit activation-quantized ANN baselines and approach 8-bit ANN baselines on ImageNet. They also preserve SNNs' low-power advantage with up to a 4.38× theoretical energy…

shortlist.title: Maternal and early life obesity programs CD4+ T cell fate to impair vaccine immunity
shortlist.abstract: In their first 3 years, children experience an average of 14 infections and receive vaccines against roughly 15 pathogens, yet whether maternal and early life obesity alters adaptive immune responses during this critical period remains largely undefined. Using a mouse model that mirrored the epidemiological link between maternal and childhood obesity, we found that high-fat diet exposure during pregnancy or early postnatal life, but not adulthood, reshaped the epigenetic and transcriptional landscape of naive CD4+ T cells and impaired their ability to differentiate into T follicular helper (TFH) cells and support germinal center reactions in response to mRNA-based and protein-based vaccines. Mechanistically, epigenetic repression of the ubiquitin-editing enzyme A20 (Tnfaip3) was a central driver of these defects. Pediatric patients with haploinsufficiency of A20 displayed a marked reduction in circulating TFH cells. Altogether, these findings establish maternal and early life obesity as determinants of adaptive immunity during a critical developmental window. Henao-Mejia and colleagues show that a high-fat diet during pregnancy or early postnatal life impairs CD4+ TFH cell differentiation and germinal center reactions in response to vaccination in young mice.

The endogenously cleaved form of tau microtubule binding region containing the residue 243 (eMTBR-tau243) can be detected in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and blood and has been associated with AD tau pathology, but its specificity and biological interpretation in non-AD tauopathies remains unclear. shortlist.title: Exploring the distributional implications of targeted residential electrification in California
shortlist.abstract: The economics of residential electrification in high-cost electricity regions remain uncertain. Using metered data from over 20,000 California homes, we assess the economic, environmental, and equity impacts of end-use electrification under rollout strategies based on household income and gas infrastructure age. Even under favorable electricity rates, only 15% of households achieve positive net present values (NPVs). Cost-effectiveness improves with deeper electrification scenarios, particularly when more costs are shifted to fixed charges and for homes with existing air conditioning—54–67% of these households break even when electrifying space heating, compared to fewer than 5% of those without. Income-based rebates more than double the share of low- and moderate-income households with positive NPVs. Prioritizing areas with aging gas infrastructure yields emissions reductions on par with high-income-led adoption and avoids costly pipeline replacement, but requires the highest subsidy to achieve cost-effectiveness across all households. These findings highlight trade-offs in designing equitable electrification strategies.

HOPO 14-1, an oral form of 3,4,3-LI(1,2-HOPO), is the first shelf-stable, broad-spectrum actinide chelator in clinical development that does not require intravenous access or trained personnel. In preclinical models, 3,4,3-LI(1,2-HOPO) removed a broad range of actinides, and its oral route supports scalable emergency medical use. Objective: To evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetic parameters, and excretion of a single dose of HOPO 14-1 in healthy adults. Design, Setting, and Participants: This was a phase 1 nonrandomized clinical trial including 42 healthy adults (6 per dose level) with evaluations for 14 days after administration of a single dose and conducted at a single site in the US. Participants were recruited and screened between March 2023 and July 2025 and follow-up was completed in August 2025. Main Outcomes and Measures: The primary outcomes were the incidence and severity of adverse events, drug-related adverse events, and serious adverse events. The secondary outcomes were plasma pharmacokinetic parameters and cumulative urinary and fecal excretion. Deadly Disease, Fear, and Ostracism in the Credit Market
shortlist.abstract: This paper exploits the 2014 U.S. Ebola outbreak as a natural experiment to examine how fear distorts mortgage credit allocation. We find a 3.8-percentage-point increase in mortgage denial rates for Black applicants during the outbreak, despite negligible infection risk. Approved Black borrowers have stronger credit profiles and lower default rates, yet are less likely to receive loan modifications when delinquent. These effects are absent in algorithm-driven FinTech lending and reverse quickly postoutbreak—patterns inconsistent with statistical discrimination. Robustness tests rule out alternative explanations related to political cycles, labor market impacts, applicant pool composition changes, and bank financial conditions. Consistent with diagnostic expectation theory, higher exposure to Ebola fear does not result in a significant learning effect during the COVID-19 pandemic. shortlist.title: Long-term development of a motor memory
shortlist.abstract: Human behaviour is developed through continuous adaptation to our environment over a range of timescales. Extensive studies have investigated the mechanisms and computations underlying this process of sensorimotor adaptation using several hundred trials. However, most of our motor skills have had countless hours of practice. Here we study a simple motor adaptation task using thousands of training trials over multiple weeks to study the long-term development of a motor memory, and examine changes in adaptation, retention, interlimb transfer, decay, spontaneous recovery and generalization. Unlike previous studies, participants showed near complete compensation to the novel dynamics, along with long-term increases in retention and spontaneous recovery. Moreover, we find narrowing in the angular generalization, suggesting continual tuning of the motor memory to the task. This demonstrates the extensive changes occurring with longer training of motor tasks, highlighting their importance in studies of sensorimotor control, rehabilitation and training.

shortlist.title: Generational gains in cognitive capacity and dementia incidence rates in Western countries
shortlist.abstract: Dementia incidence has been declining in Western societies for decades, but whether this reflects higher cognitive capacity entering old age, slower cognitive decline, or both remains unresolved. Analysing ~783,000 episodic memory assessments from ~219,000 individuals across five longitudinal cohorts, we find that later-born cohorts benefit from a double dividend: higher memory levels entering old age and slower rates of decline. The projected 20-year cohort advantage at age 80 is of sufficient magnitude to plausibly account for the observed 13% per-decade decline in dementia incidence reported in meta-analyses. Generational gains are disproportionately concentrated among the fastest-declining individuals, and are reflected in lower hippocampal atrophy rates in an independent sample. A formal bounding analysis shows that the double dividend is robust across a range of plausible period assumptions, consistent with environmental conditions operating across the lifespan having reshaped the architecture of human cognitive aging.

shortlist.title: Resistance exercise to attenuate lean mass loss during tirzepatide therapy for obesity: a randomized controlled trial
shortlist.abstract: Incretin mimetics as obesity therapy induce substantial weight and fat loss but also decrease lean soft tissue mass, possibly impairing skeletal muscle function. Here, in this two-arm randomized controlled trial of adding resistance exercise (REx) to tirzepatide (T), 120 adults with overweight or obesity were treated with tirzepatide and randomized to thrice-weekly resistance exercise training or usual activities for 40 weeks. Tirzepatide was safe, and most participants tolerated up-titration to 15 mg weekly. Adherence to resistance exercise was 91%. Weight loss achieved was similar (T = -22.61 kg, T+REx = -22.28 kg, P = 0.694). For primary outcomes, loss of total fat mass was similar (T = -17.19 kg, T+REx = -17.98 kg, P = 0.700; between-group difference = -0.77 kg, 95% confidence interval (CI): -2.14 kg to 0.60 kg), but resistance exercise reduced loss of total lean soft tissue mass (T = -4.67 kg, T+REx = -3.57 kg, P < 0.001; between-group difference = 1.09 kg, 95% CI: 0.43-1.75 kg). For related endpoints, resistance exercise reduced loss of appendicular lean soft tissue mass (T = -3.55 kg, T+REx = -2.92 kg, P < 0.001). Upper and lower body muscle strength decreased with tirzepatide (bench press -4.09 kg, lat pulldown -4.42 kg, knee extension -4.42 kg) but increased with T+REx (+4.68 kg, +8.58 kg, +5.88 kg, respectively, all P < 0.001 versus tirzepatide). In conclusion, resistance exercise training attenuated loss of total lean soft tissue mass, representing an effective adjunct to tirzepatide anti-obesity therapy. shortlist.title: How Sociotropic Aesthetic Judgments Drive Opposition to Dense Housing Development
shortlist.abstract: Voter opposition to dense housing development contributes to America’s housing shortage. Prevailing explanations emphasize homeowner self-interest and “NIMBYism.” We develop a theory of how sociotropic aesthetic judgments shape housing policy preferences and demonstrate its unique implications with a series of descriptive studies and experiments. First, people who choose to live in dense neighborhoods have an aesthetic taste for density, leading homeowners in already-dense areas to be more supportive of dense development both in their neighborhoods and elsewhere. Second, voters are more supportive of dense development when it is proposed in already-dense neighborhoods where it “fits”—even voters who live in those same dense neighborhoods. Finally, genuine aesthetic distaste for tall buildings is widespread and causally affects support for development. Our findings offer a new lens for understanding housing policy preferences and suggest novel solutions for addressing America’s housing shortage.

From Design to Disclosure
shortlist.abstract: We study the role of hard information in contractual and market settings in which the receiver can flexibly adjust allocations and transfers in response to the sender's disclosure. These settings include monopoly pricing, insurance contracting, and policy negotiations. Across these settings, the sender is worst off if she reveals her type completely because the receiver would then adjust the terms of trade to extract her surplus. Taking this feature as our central departure from the literature, we characterize the entire set of equilibrium payoffs in these disclosure games. We prove an equivalence result: a payoff profile can be approximated by an equilibrium of the disclosure game if and only if it can be achieved through information design. Thus, there exist equilibria in which the sender obtains approximately her commitment payoff.

shortlist.title: Do Fund Managers’ Commitments to Responsible Investing Affect Private Information Acquisition, Information Environment, and Corporate Sustainability?
shortlist.abstract: We investigate the effects of mutual funds’ commitments to responsible investing on their information acquisition activities and the corresponding externalities for other stakeholders. After committing to responsible investing (via United Nations Principles for Responsible Investment (UNPRI)), fund managers increase private information acquisition activities, that is, corporate site visits, particularly focusing on environmental and social issues. These visits generate negligible private investment value for the visiting funds. However, the information environment at the stock level improves following these visits with lower consensus analyst forecast errors. In addition to the information production role of these visits, they also generate positive externalities for other stakeholders through incremental improvements in the sustainability practices of the firms receiving sustainability-focused site visits from UNPRI fund managers. Collectively, the paper highlights the private costs and social benefits of responsible investing. This paper was accepted by Will Cong, finance. Funding: S. Agarwal and J. shortlist.abstract: We analyze novel data on corporate contributions to ballot initiatives at the U.S. state level. Firms make large contributions to ballot measure campaigns in favor of or against specific initiatives. They contribute significantly more to business initiatives compared with ideological initiatives. Corporate campaign spending is systematically associated with the likelihood that a ballot measure passes. Contributing firms experience changes in sales growth following the passage of important ballot measures. Following successful (failed) initiatives, all firms in affected industries exhibit significantly more positive (negative) cumulative abnormal returns around the election, but contributing firms do more so than peers. shortlist.title: Conserved T cell receptor usage underpins recognition of CD1c presenting a mycobacterial lipid
shortlist.abstract: The mechanism by which αβ T cell receptors (TCRs) recognize mycobacterial lipids presented by CD1 family members is not well understood. We used CD1c tetramers loaded with the mycobacterial phosphomycoketide (PM) or mannosyl-PM to isolate T cells from healthy blood donors and individuals from a tuberculosis (TB)-endemic region of South Africa, with higher frequencies observed in individuals from the TB-endemic region. High-throughput analysis of >200 paired CD1c–mycoketide tetramer+ αβTCRs identified a conserved TCR motif, encoded by TRBV4-1 or TRBV7-9 variable region genes in greater than half of TCRs sequenced. A cryo-EM structure of a TRBV7-9+ TCR in complex with CD1c-PM demonstrated that the TCR bound to the A′-side of CD1c, directly contacting the phospholipid antigen and F′-portal residues. Analysis of multiple T cell clones interacting with CD1c mutants suggested that this TCR docking mode is representative of the larger TRBV7-9+ T cell population. Collectively, this study provides insight into mycobacterial lipid antigen recognition by αβ T cells restricted to CD1c.

fundamentals.title: Fluctuation-Response Theory of Nonequilibrium Complex Fluids
fundamentals.abstract: A fundamental challenge in soft matter physics is to describe materials, such as the living cytoplasm and tissues, that are simultaneously active, chemically driven, and exhibit long-lasting memory of mechanical stresses. Here, we construct a generalized hydrodynamic framework at finite wave vectors and frequencies that is applicable to nonequilibrium fluids with memory. By leveraging stationary correlation identities, we derive a generalized linear response theory for nonequilibrium steady states. This framework serves as a formal extension of Onsager’s regression hypothesis beyond thermal equilibrium. Our approach provides a direct pathway to derive transport coefficients from steady-state fluctuations without the traditional Mori-Zwanzig projection-operator formalism, generalizing the Green-Kubo relations to nonequilibrium systems. As a corollary, we derive two model-free variants of the nonequilibrium fluctuation-response relation for non-Markovian dynamics. These generalized relations explicitly capture the nonequilibrium circulating currents—an out-of-equilibrium signature that is invisible to conventional scalar formulations or frameworks that treat degrees of freedom independently. Applying our theory to chemically driven active fluids reveals the emergence of active viscoelastic memory, wherein chemical reaction cycles dynamically renormalize the macroscopic viscous response. Strikingly, this active memory can induce negative storage modulus at finite frequencies, a behavior absent in ordinary viscoelastic fluids. Our first-principles framework rigorously extends linear rheology to nonequilibrium systems and provides a foundation for understanding non-Markovian dynamics across a broad range of biological and synthetic active matter.

fundamentals.title: Origin of Electride States and Their Responses under Pressure
fundamentals.abstract: Electrides are unique materials in which electrons occupy interstitial regions formed by cation frameworks and act as anions. They have many interesting properties and are often induced by high pressure in some materials. Understanding the emergence of electride states is a central problem in condensed-matter physics. While existing theoretical frameworks, including the interstitial quasi-atom (ISQ) and electron-ion interaction (EII) models, have provided some useful phenomenological interpretations of the electride formation, the atomistic origin and the underlying physics of this charge redistribution remain unclear. Here, within a first-principles framework, we systematically study the evolution of electronic structures of compressed materials, using alkali metals as representative examples. By mapping symmetry-resolved electronic band states onto atomic orbitals, we find that (i) pressure-induced quantum confinement raises the energies of atomic orbitals due to enhanced kinetic energy and increased overlap between valence and core electrons, with the energy shift being larger for more delocalized s orbital than for more localized p and d orbitals; and (ii) this effect causes reordering of band states, making the electride states, which are composed of the interatomic hybridized pd orbitals, to progressively shift in energy below the s orbital states, leading to their occupation and the onset of electride behavior. This microscopic electronic-state picture clarifies the origin of the electride formation and provides a general framework for understanding the evolution of interstitial electronic states under compression across diverse materials.

fundamentals.title: Spectral Small-Incremental Entangling: Breaking Quasipolynomial Complexity Barriers in Long-Range Interacting Systems
fundamentals.abstract: How the detailed entanglement structure emerges from quantum dynamics remains a fundamental challenge motivated by recent advances in quantum simulators and information processing. As a central milestone, the small-incremental-entangling (SIE) theorem bounds the entanglement-entropy growth rate but does not control the entanglement spectrum itself. In this work, we define the spectral-entangling strength, which quantifies how strongly an operator can reshape the distribution of Schmidt coefficients across a bipartition. We then prove a spectral-SIE theorem: for Rényi index α ≥ 1 / 2 , the growth rate of Rényi-entanglement entropies admits a universal bound. Remarkably, our bound at α = 1 / 2 is both qualitatively and quantitatively optimal; below this threshold ( α < 1 / 2 ), no universal speed limit on entanglement growth can exist. This result yields a sharp 1 / s 2 threshold in the tail of the ordered squared Schmidt coefficients, or equivalently in the entanglement-spectrum weights (with s the Schmidt index). It enables rigorous truncation-based-error control and establishes a quantitative link between entanglement-spectrum structure and computational complexity. As a practical highlight, for one-dimensional power-law interactions 1 / r η with η > 2 , this implies matrix-product-state approximations with bond dimension polynomial in ( n / ε ) for ground states, real-time evolved states, and Gibbs states, thereby closing the quasipolynomial gap, where n is the system size, and ε denotes the target approximation error in the relevant state or operator norm. By controlling Rényi entanglement, we further obtain a rigorous truncation-error bound for the time-dependent density-matrix renormalization-group scheme analyzed here. fundamentals.title: Dual Relaxation Modes Control Polymer Crystallization
fundamentals.abstract: Crystallization in polymers provides a fundamental probe of how molecular relaxation governs the emergence of order in glass-forming systems. Despite the longstanding success of the Lauritzen-Hoffman theory, its empirical treatment of molecular diffusion fails to capture the crystallization kinetics observed in the deeply supercooled regime. Here, we establish a physically grounded framework that replaces the empirical mobility in the Lauritzen-Hoffman formalism with a weighted combination of two measurable relaxation modes, namely the structural α relaxation, governing cooperative dynamics, and the slow Arrhenius process, associated with localized molecular rearrangements. This unified two-channel description quantitatively reproduces crystallization kinetics over several decades in time across 12 polymers spanning a wide range of fragility. In addition, our framework remains predictive under nanoconfinement, where interfaces and finite-size effects modify both mobility and nucleation. The results reveal that polymer crystallization proceeds through coupled long-range transport and localized ordering events governed by the same relaxation hierarchy that underlies vitrification, thus bridging glassy dynamics and crystallization kinetics at the molecular level.

fundamentals.title: Ordering of oxygen atoms in titanium revealed by superresolution electron ptychography
fundamentals.abstract: Interstitial atoms such as oxygen, carbon, and nitrogen are common point defects in crystalline solids and play important roles in determining electronic and mechanical properties. For decades, their behavior has been modeled assuming random spatial distributions owing to the lack of direct experimental access to their atomic-scale arrangements. Here, using oxygen-doped α-titanium as a model system, we overcome this fundamental limitation by achieving the first three-dimensional visualization, quantitative counting, and sub-[˚]Angstr¨om positioning of individual interstitial oxygen atoms in the bulk, enabled by super-resolution 4D-STEM ptychography with an adaptive prop agator. We find that interstitial oxygen atoms do not distribute randomly; instead, they exhibit correlated occupancy along the [0001] direction, giving rise to nanoscale ordered domains that are not detectable by conventional imaging. This discovery overturns the long-standing paradigm of randomness in interstitial systems and provides a microscopic foundation for understanding anomalous transport, strengthening, and phase stability in interstitial-engineered materials. Our approach establishes a general platform for atomic-scale defect metrology, opening avenues to ratio nally design materials through precise control of interstitial architectures in metals, semiconductors, and quantum solids.
fundamentals.topic: Advanced Electron Microscopy Techniques and Applications

fundamentals.title: Unramified Gromov–Witten and Gopakumar–Vafa invariants
fundamentals.journal: Journal of the American Mathematical Society
fundamentals.abstract: Kim, Kresch, and Oh defined unramified Gromov–Witten invariants. For threefolds, Pandharipande conjectured that these invariants are equal to the Gopakumar–Vafa invariants for Fano curve classes and primitive Calabi–Yau classes. We prove the conjecture using a wall-crossing method developed here. As a result, we obtain an algebro-geometric construction of Gopakumar–Vafa invariants in these cases.

fundamentals.title: The Huang–Yang conjecture for the low-density Fermi gas
fundamentals.abstract: Our work establishes a three-term asymptotic expansion of the ground state energy of a dilute gas of spin 1/2 1 / 2 fermions with repulsive short-range interactions, validating a formula predicted by Huang and Yang in 1957. The formula is universal in the sense that it holds for a large class of interaction potentials and depends on those only via their scattering length. We have recently proved an upper bound on the ground state energy of the desired form, and the present work completes the program by proving the matching lower bound.
fundamentals.topic: Cold Atom Physics and Bose-Einstein Condensates

fundamentals.title: Necessary and sufficient conditions for universality limits
fundamentals.abstract: We derive necessary and sufficient conditions for universality limits for orthogonal polynomials associated to a fixed measure on the real line and related systems. One of our results is that the Christoffel–Darboux kernel has sine kernel asymptotics at a point ξ ξ , with regularly varying scaling, if and only if the orthogonality measure (spectral measure) has a unique tangent measure at ξ ξ and that tangent measure is the Lebesgue measure. All previously known cases of sine kernel asymptotics, with absolutely continuous or singular measures, have regularly varying scaling. Our work is not limited to bulk universality; we show that the Christoffel–Darboux kernel has a regularly varying scaling limit with a nontrivial limit kernel if and only if the orthogonality measure has a unique tangent measure at ξ ξ and that tangent measure is not a point mass. The possible limit kernels correspond to homogeneous de Branges spaces; in particular, this equivalence completely characterizes several prominent universality classes such as hard edge universality, Fisher–Hartwig singularities, and jump discontinuities in the weights. A key ingredient in the proof is a new correspondence between measures and chains of de Branges spaces, not between Weyl functions and Hamiltonians. In order to handle limits with power law weights, this correspondence goes beyond the more common setting of Poisson-finite measures, and allows arbitrary power bounded measures.

fundamentals.title: The Limit of Nature: Thucydides and the Politics of Theory
fundamentals.abstract: This article reconsiders Thucydides’s role as a foundational theorist of human nature. Contrary to conventional readings, I argue that Thucydides approaches “nature” ( physis ) less as a universal principle of behavior than as a site of political and theoretical investigation. By distinguishing his authorial voice from those of his speakers, I demonstrate that his analysis consistently approaches human nature as a limit concept—a baseline and boundary of human capacity that emerges in moments of existential precarity—while introducing a more nuanced set of terms to describe the habitual behaviors of political groups. By nevertheless foregrounding the more robust and determinative concept of nature in moments of contentious deliberation, Thucydides encourages reflection on the political dynamics that generate essentialist theories in public discourse. His account thus serves as a helpful point of reference for thinking about how competitive, polarizing speech affects the substantive categories of political debate and analysis, and through them political action.

fundamentals.title: Similarity Solutions of Shock Formation for First-Order Strictly Hyperbolic Systems
fundamentals.abstract: Shocks due to hyperbolic partial differential equations (PDEs) appear throughout mathematics and science. The canonical example is shock formation in the inviscid Burgers equation [Formula: see text]. Previous studies have shown that when shocks form for the inviscid Burgers equation, for positions and times close to the shock singularity, the dynamics are locally self-similar and universal, i.e., dynamics are equivalent regardless of the initial conditions. In this paper, we show that, in fact, shock formation is self-similar and universal for general first-order strictly hyperbolic PDEs in one spatial dimension, and the self-similarity is like that of the inviscid Burgers equation. An analytical formula is derived for the self-similar universal solution. Reproducibility of computational results. This paper has been awarded the “SIAM Reproducibility Badge: Code and data available” as a recognition that the authors have followed reproducibility principles valued by SIREV and the scientific computing community. Code and data that allow readers to reproduce the results in this paper are available at https://doi.org/10.34770/6vgh-br25 and in the supplementary materials ( M180373_SM.zip [25.7MB]). [Formula: see text]

fundamentals.title: Uncovering internal sensory evidence reveals the nature of confidence computation in multi-alternative perceptual decision making.
fundamentals.abstract: A central goal of perceptual decision making is to determine the computations underlying choice and confidence in complex, multi-alternative tasks. However, revealing these computations requires knowledge of the internal sensory evidence upon which the computations operate. Unfortunately, unlike for two-choice tasks, there is no established method in multi-alternative tasks to determine how stimuli are transformed into internal sensory evidence. Here we address this critical gap by developing a novel modeling paradigm that reveals how the brain transforms external stimuli into internal sensory evidence during multi-alternative decision making in the context of numerosity tasks. Across three experiments that feature two-, three-, and five-choice conditions, we show that the internal sensory evidence in our numerosity task can be described with a simple, two-parameter equation that fits data for up to 12 conditions. Critically, the ability to model the internal sensory evidence allowed us to test six theories of confidence computation. Our results support a model where confidence reflects the raw evidence difference between the top two alternatives. These results establish a new numerosity paradigm in which a two-parameter equation can be used to determine the internal sensory evidence for a potentially unlimited number of multi-alternative conditions and reveal the confidence computation in multi-alternative tasks.
